## Overview

BMW's corporate site carries a far more **measured, corporate-automotive** interface than its motorsport-bombastic cousin BMW M. The atmosphere is light: `{colors.canvas}` (#ffffff) is the base surface, `{colors.surface-card}` (#fafafa) carries the soft-grey card plates, and dark navy `{colors.surface-dark}` (#1a2129) appears only inside hero bands — one per page, framing the lead model render.

Type runs BMW's licensed **BMW Type Next Latin** at two weights: heavy 700 (display + button + nav) and Light 300 (body + secondary copy). That contrast — heavy display next to thin paragraph — is the editorial signature, channeling the brand's "European-engineered" voice. Weight 500 is deliberately absent; weight 400 only appears on caption and nav-link in neutral utility contexts.

The brand action color, **BMW corporate blue** (`{colors.primary}` — #1c69d4), works alone across every primary CTA — buttons are **rectangular, 0px corner**, with white type. The site rotates a blue-button + dark-navy-hero combination across page rhythm. The M tricolor stripe (`{colors.m-blue-light}` → `{colors.m-blue-dark}` → `{colors.m-red}`) only appears in motorsport contexts and as M-model badges/dividers — never in the corporate site's main language.

The configuration and reservation flows add a dealer-side inventory UI on top of the same system — filter chips, model cards, price tables — but typography and color stay identical; only density goes up.

**Key Characteristics:**
- Light `{colors.canvas}` is the base surface; dark navy `{colors.surface-dark}` appears only inside hero bands — page rhythm relies on contrast.
- BMW corporate blue (`{colors.primary}` — #1c69d4) acts as the single primary action color.
- BMW Type Next Latin: weight 700 display against weight 300 body is the signature.
- Buttons are **rectangular, 0px radius** — corporate dialect, distinct from M's sportier radii.
- Model cards run as 4-up or 5-up grids with no hairline border or only minimal border — just white plate + photo + title.
- Photography (model renders) sits in environment, no shadow — depth comes entirely from color-block contrast.
- M tricolor stripe appears only in M-model contexts — not part of the corporate language.
- Section rhythm holds at `{spacing.section}` (80px) for every major band.

## Colors

### Brand & Accent
- **BMW Blue (Primary)** (`{colors.primary}` — #1c69d4): The single brand action color. All primary CTAs, "Learn More" link prefixes (blue text), nav-link active state. Press shifts to `{colors.primary-active}` (#0653b6).
- **M Blue Light** (`{colors.m-blue-light}` — #0066b1) + **M Blue Dark** (`{colors.m-blue-dark}` — #1c69d4) + **M Red** (`{colors.m-red}` — #e22718): The M tricolor stripe — appears on the corporate site only on M-model pages and the "M" badge. Never as CTA colors.

### Surface
- **Canvas** (`{colors.canvas}` — #ffffff): The default page surface.
- **Surface Soft** (`{colors.surface-soft}` — #f7f7f7): Soft grey for the footer and sub-navigation bands.
- **Surface Card** (`{colors.surface-card}` — #fafafa): The light plate behind a model card's photo block.
- **Surface Strong** (`{colors.surface-strong}` — #ebebeb): A slightly heavier grey used as a section divider.
- **Surface Dark** (`{colors.surface-dark}` — #1a2129): Dark navy for hero bands and large dark CTAs. Not pure black — carries a warm undertone.
- **Surface Dark Elevated** (`{colors.surface-dark-elevated}` — #262e38): One step lighter, used for nested cards on top of the dark hero.

### Hairlines
- **Hairline** (`{colors.hairline}` — #e6e6e6): The 1px divider — input outline, configurator card outline, table separator.
- **Hairline Strong** (`{colors.hairline-strong}` — #cccccc): A more visible 1px outline — disabled secondary buttons, emphasized table border.

### Text
- **Ink** (`{colors.ink}` — #262626): All display and primary text. Not pure black — soft against photography.
- **Body** (`{colors.body}` — #3c3c3c): Default running text.
- **Body Strong** (`{colors.body-strong}` — #1a1a1a): Emphasized paragraphs and lead text.
- **Muted** (`{colors.muted}` — #6b6b6b): Footer links, breadcrumbs, captions.
- **Muted Soft** (`{colors.muted-soft}` — #9a9a9a): Disabled text, fine-print legal.
- **On Primary** (`{colors.on-primary}` — #ffffff): White text on a blue button.
- **On Dark** (`{colors.on-dark}` — #ffffff): White text on a dark hero band.
- **On Dark Soft** (`{colors.on-dark-soft}` — #bbbbbb): A slightly muted white for secondary text on dark bands.

### Semantic
- **Success** (`{colors.success}` — #22c55e): Confirmation messages and "available" indicators.
- **Warning** (`{colors.warning}` — #f59e0b): Warning callouts.
- **Error** (`{colors.error}` — #dc2626): Validation errors.

## Typography

### Font Family
The system runs **BMW Type Next Latin** in two cuts: regular (display + UI labels) and **BMW Type Next Latin Light** (body + secondary copy). Fallback stack: `system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif`.

The display/body split is functional:
- BMW Type Next Latin (700) → display headlines, button labels, nav links
- BMW Type Next Latin Light (300) → paragraphs, descriptive copy
- BMW Type Next Latin (400) → caption, neutral nav-link contexts

This three-way split mirrors BMW M's — corporate and the M sub-brand share the same typographic DNA; only the weight/size ratios differ.

### Hierarchy

| Token | Size | Weight | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{typography.display-xl}` | 64px | 700 | 1.05 | 0 | Hero h1 ("iX3", model name) |
| `{typography.display-lg}` | 48px | 700 | 1.1 | 0 | Section heads |
| `{typography.display-md}` | 32px | 700 | 1.15 | 0 | Sub-section heads |
| `{typography.display-sm}` | 24px | 700 | 1.25 | 0 | CTA-band headlines |
| `{typography.title-lg}` | 20px | 700 | 1.3 | 0 | Card group titles |
| `{typography.title-md}` | 18px | 700 | 1.4 | 0 | Model card title, intro paragraphs |
| `{typography.title-sm}` | 16px | 700 | 1.4 | 0 | Inventory card title, list label |
| `{typography.body-md}` | 16px | 300 (Light) | 1.55 | 0 | Default body — BMW Type Next Latin Light |
| `{typography.body-sm}` | 14px | 300 (Light) | 1.55 | 0 | Footer body, fine-print |
| `{typography.caption}` | 12px | 400 | 1.4 | 0.5px | Photo captions, meta |
| `{typography.label-uppercase}` | 13px | 700 | 1.3 | 1.5px | "LEARN MORE" inline links, category tabs |
| `{typography.button}` | 14px | 700 | 1.0 | 0.5px | Standard CTA button label |
| `{typography.nav-link}` | 14px | 400 | 1.4 | 0.3px | Top-nav menu items |

### Principles
- The **700/300 contrast** is the editorial signature. Weight 500 is absent from the system.
- **No negative letter-spacing** — BMW Type Next Latin works on a wide body, so tracking stays at default. Apple/Cal.com-style tightening reads off-brand here.
- **UPPERCASE inline links** — "LEARN MORE"-style CTAs run uppercase with 1.5px tracking. The "machined precision" voice.
- **Weight 400 lives in a narrow lane** — only caption and nav-link, both neutral utility roles.

### Note on Font Substitutes
BMW Type Next Latin is a licensed BMW typeface. Open-source alternatives:
- **Inter** (variable) — close match at weight 700/300. Leave letter-spacing at 0.0em.
- **Saira Condensed** — for a slightly more compressed BMW Type feel.

## Layout

### Spacing System
- **Base unit:** 8px.
- **Tokens:** `{spacing.xxs}` 4px · `{spacing.xs}` 8px · `{spacing.sm}` 12px · `{spacing.md}` 16px · `{spacing.lg}` 24px · `{spacing.xl}` 32px · `{spacing.xxl}` 48px · `{spacing.section}` 80px.
- **Section padding:** `{spacing.section}` (80px) for every major editorial band.
- **Card internal padding:** `{spacing.lg}` (24px) for model and feature cards.

### Grid & Container
- **Max content width:** ~1440px center-aligned.
- **Editorial body:** A single 12-column grid.
- **Model card grids:** 4-up or 5-up at desktop, 2-up at tablet, 1-up on mobile.
- **Configurator inventory grids:** 3-up filter row + 4-up vehicle cards, dense layout.

### Whitespace Philosophy
BMW's whitespace strategy is tighter than BMW M's motorsport-aerated grenadier — the corporate side is more utility-driven. Section rhythm is 80px (not M's 96px). Card padding is 24px (not M's 32px). The page is denser, more dealership-functional.

## Elevation & Depth

| Level | Treatment | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Flat | No shadow, no border | Body, top nav, footer, hero bands |
| Soft hairline | 1px `{colors.hairline}` border | Configurator option tile, table divider |
| Card surface | `{colors.surface-card}` background — no shadow | Model card photo plate |
| Photographic | Edge-to-edge photography | Hero band, model renders |

The system never uses a drop shadow. Depth comes entirely from (a) color-block contrast (light canvas vs dark hero) and (b) photographic subject + lighting.

### Decorative Depth
- **`m-stripe-divider`** — a 4px-tall horizontal tricolor stripe (`{colors.m-blue-light}` → `{colors.m-blue-dark}` → `{colors.m-red}`). Only in M-model contexts, motorsport badges, or as an M-related section divider. Not part of the main corporate flow.
- **Photographic depth** — full-bleed vehicle photography (lighting + subject) does the work chrome would otherwise do.

## Shapes

### Border Radius Scale

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `{rounded.none}` | 0px | Every button, card, input, configurator chip — the dominant radius |
| `{rounded.xs}` | 2px | Very small badges, very rare |
| `{rounded.sm}` | 4px | Small inline button (rare) |
| `{rounded.md}` | 8px | Mobile-only collapse cards (rare) |
| `{rounded.lg}` | 12px | Very rare — modal/dialog corners |
| `{rounded.pill}` | 9999px | Filter chips in some contexts (rare) |
| `{rounded.full}` | 9999px / 50% | Avatar, circular icon button |

The radius hierarchy is binary: **rectangular for everything, circular only for icon buttons.** A clear departure from the soft-cornered SaaS dialect of Apple or Cal.com — closer to BMW corporate-automotive's "engineered precision" voice.

### Photography Geometry
- Hero photography is full-bleed at 16:9 or 21:9 cinematic ratio.
- Model card photos sit at 16:10, edge-to-edge with `{rounded.none}` corners.
- Configurator vehicle renders sit on a white studio background, full silhouette visible.

## Components

### Top Navigation

**`top-nav`** — A white sticky nav bar pinned to the top of the page. 64px tall, `{colors.canvas}` background. Left: BMW circular badge logo; center: primary horizontal menu (Models, Next Generation, Pre-Owned, Dealers, Test Drive); right: cart icon, language picker, profile. Menu items render in `{typography.nav-link}` (14px / 400 / 0.3px tracking).

### Buttons

**`button-primary`** — The signature primary CTA. Background `{colors.primary}` (BMW Blue #1c69d4), text `{colors.on-primary}`, type `{typography.button}` (BMW Type Next Latin 14px / 700 / 0.5px tracking), padding 14px × 32px, height 48px, rounded `{rounded.none}` (0px — rectangular). Press state: `button-primary-active` shifts to `{colors.primary-active}`.

**`button-secondary`** — A white button with a hairline outline. Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, 1px `{colors.hairline-strong}` border, same padding + height + radius.

**`button-secondary-on-dark`** — Used over a dark hero band. Background transparent, text `{colors.on-dark}`, 1px `{colors.on-dark}` border, same rectangular shape.

**`button-text-link`** — An inline UPPERCASE letter-spaced link. No background, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.label-uppercase}` (13px / 700 / 1.5px tracking). Reads as "LEARN MORE", terminated by a `›` chevron.

**`text-link`** — An inline link inside body copy. `{colors.ink}` text, no underline by default; underlines per context.

### Cards & Containers

**`hero-band-dark`** — Full-width dark navy hero. Background `{colors.surface-dark}`, text `{colors.on-dark}`, vertical padding `{spacing.section}` (80px). Centered: model name in `{typography.display-xl}` (64px / 700) + sub-headline + vehicle render (right-aligned or below). A single `{component.button-primary}` (blue) or `{component.button-secondary-on-dark}`.

**`hero-photo-band`** — A light-canvas model showcase band. Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`. The vehicle render takes the wide area; right or below, a headline + two link CTAs + sub-tagline.

**`model-card`** — Used in 4-up or 5-up model card grids on the homepage ("BMW iX3", "BMW iX", "BMW 5 Series"). Background `{colors.canvas}`, rounded `{rounded.none}`, padding `{spacing.lg}` (24px). Contents: model render at the top (`{component.model-card-photo}` on `{colors.surface-card}`), model name in `{typography.title-md}` (18px / 700) below, a one-line tagline in `{typography.body-sm}` (14px / 300), and a `{component.button-text-link}` ("LEARN MORE ›").

**`model-card-photo`** — The card's photo plate. Background `{colors.surface-card}` (#fafafa — soft grey), rounded `{rounded.none}`, vehicle render in full silhouette. Zero padding — the photo runs edge-to-edge.

**`feature-photo-card`** — A feature/lifestyle card. Background `{colors.canvas}`, padding `{spacing.lg}`. 16:9 photo at the top, `{typography.title-md}` headline + body excerpt below.

**`spec-cell`** — A technical spec cell (model detail page). Transparent background, separated by hairline dividers. Value on top (`{typography.display-sm}` 24px / 700), label below (`{typography.label-uppercase}`).

### Inventory & Configurator

**`inventory-card`** — One card per vehicle on the dealer inventory page. Background `{colors.canvas}`, padding `{spacing.md}` (16px), rounded `{rounded.none}`. Vehicle photo on top, model + variant name + price + "View" link below.

**`filter-chip`** + **`filter-chip-active`** — Inventory filter chips (model, year, price range). Inactive: background `{colors.canvas}`, 1px `{colors.hairline-strong}` border, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.caption}`. Active: background `{colors.ink}`, text `{colors.on-dark}`. Padding 8px × 14px, radius `{rounded.none}`.

**`configurator-option-tile`** + **`configurator-option-tile-selected`** — Configurator selection cell (color, wheels, upholstery). Inactive: background `{colors.canvas}`, 1px hairline. Selected: 2px `{colors.primary}` border. Padding 16px × 24px, radius `{rounded.none}`.

### Inputs & Forms

**`text-input`** — Standard text input. Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.body-md}`, rounded `{rounded.none}` (0px), padding 14px × 16px, height 48px, 1px hairline border. On focus, the border thickens to ink.

**`cookie-consent-card`** — Cookie banner. Background `{colors.canvas}`, 1px hairline, padding `{spacing.lg}` (24px), `{typography.body-sm}` (14px / 300 — Light even in legal copy).

### Tabs / Tags

**`category-tab`** + **`category-tab-active`** — Category sub-nav. Inactive: transparent + `{colors.muted}` UPPERCASE label. Active: transparent + `{colors.ink}` UPPERCASE label + 2px ink underline. 12px vertical padding, no horizontal radius.

### Brand Signature

**`m-stripe-divider`** — A 4px-tall horizontal tricolor stripe (`{colors.m-blue-light}` → `{colors.m-blue-dark}` → `{colors.m-red}`). Only in M-model contexts, motorsport badges, or as an M-related section divider. Absent from the corporate main flow; on M-model detail pages and the M Performance badge it plays an inline divider role.

### CTA / Footer

**`cta-band-photo`** — A pre-footer "Discover the New iX3"-style band. Background `{colors.surface-dark}` with a full-bleed vehicle photo. Centered headline in `{typography.display-md}` (32px / 700) + a single `{component.button-secondary-on-dark}`. 80px padding.

**`footer`** — The closing soft-grey footer. Background `{colors.surface-soft}` (#f7f7f7 — not pure white — soft grey), text `{colors.body}`. A 4-column link list: Models / Services / Dealers / About. Vertical padding 64px. Below, a copyright line in `{typography.body-sm}` with `{colors.muted}`.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do
- Sit every page on `{colors.canvas}` (pure white); reserve `{colors.surface-dark}` for hero bands only.
- Pair primary CTAs with `{colors.primary}` (BMW Blue) + `{colors.on-primary}` white text + `{rounded.none}` 0px corners — the corporate signature.
- Set display headlines in BMW Type Next Latin 700 and body in Light 300. The contrast is non-negotiable.
- Use UPPERCASE letter-spaced links like "LEARN MORE" as inline CTAs.
- Place the model card photo on `{colors.surface-card}` with the title beneath — the standard BMW corporate pattern.
- Hold section rhythm at `{spacing.section}` (80px) — tighter than BMW M's 96px.
- Reserve the M tricolor stripe for M-model contexts and motorsport dividers.

### Don't
- Don't add a brand color other than blue — BMW Blue is the only primary action color.
- Don't use pill or rounded buttons — `{rounded.none}` (0px) rectangular IS the brand button.
- Don't drop display weight to 500 — the system uses 700 / 400 / 300; 500 is absent.
- Don't bold body type — Light 300 is the BMW corporate editorial voice.
- Don't add drop shadows to cards — depth comes from photo + color-block contrast.
- Don't repeat the same surface mode across two consecutive bands — light → dark hero → light → light feature → dark CTA → light footer rotation is required.
- Don't use the M tricolor stripe as a CTA fill — divider/accent role only.
- Don't mix languages in a single page — UI language must stay consistent.

## Responsive Behavior

### Breakpoints

| Name | Width | Key Changes |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile | < 768px | Hamburger nav; hero h1 64→40px; model card grid 1-up; configurator filter chips 2-up; footer 4 col → 1 col |
| Tablet | 768–1024px | Top nav narrows, secondary menu hides under "More"; model card 2-up; inventory 2-up |
| Desktop | 1024–1440px | Full top-nav; 4-up or 5-up model card grid; inventory 3-up; full configurator UI |
| Wide | > 1440px | Same as desktop, content fixed at 1440px; gutters absorb the rest |

### Touch Targets
- `{component.button-primary}` minimum 48 × 48px — above WCAG AAA (44 × 44).
- `{component.text-input}` height 48px.
- Category tabs run with 12px vertical padding, giving an effective tap area > 44px.

### Collapsing Strategy
- The top nav collapses to a hamburger below 768px; the menu opens as a full-screen sheet.
- The hero band's internal layout drops to a single column.
- Model card grid 4-up/5-up → 2-up → 1-up.
- The configurator filter chip row scrolls horizontally on mobile.
- The M tricolor stripe stays at 4px height across every breakpoint.

### Image Behavior
- Model renders scale at every breakpoint while preserving native aspect ratios.
- Hero photography may shift to a more vertical crop on mobile (art direction).
- Inventory vehicle photos may move from 16:9 to 4:3 on mobile.

## Iteration Guide

1. Focus on a single component. Reference its YAML key directly (`{component.model-card}`, `{component.button-primary}`).
2. New components default to `{rounded.none}` (0px). Use `{rounded.full}` only for circular icon buttons.
3. Variants (`-active`, `-disabled`, `-selected`) live as separate entries inside the `components:` block.
4. `{token.refs}` everywhere — never inline hex.
5. Hover state is never documented. Only Default and Active/Pressed states.
6. Display headlines stay BMW Type Next Latin 700; body stays Light 300; the trio is fixed.
7. Keep UI strings in a single language — match the locale of the page.

## Known Gaps

- BMW Type Next Latin is licensed to BMW and not published as a public web font; Inter at weights 700/300 is documented as the substitute.
- Animation and transition timings (configurator color swap, model card hover-reveal) are out of scope here.
- Form validation states beyond `{component.text-input}` focus were not extracted — error/success states would need a dedicated form page.
- The dealer inventory sub-domain shares typography and color with the main corporate site; only UI density rises (filters, tables, prices).
- A cookie consent overlay can occlude part of the hero — the lead hero band content may not be fully captured.
- The M tricolor stripe appears infrequently on this corporate site; full motorsport context lives on the BMW M site.
# UI design guidelines

Project-specific adaptation of the supplied `design-taste-frontend` guidance.
Read alongside [`../design.md`](../design.md), which defines the BMW design system.

## Scope and precedence

Use BMW tokens for every generated UI. Apply the marketing-page guidance below to landing
pages, portfolios, editorial pages, and redesigns. Do not impose marketing hero, photography,
section variety, or short-copy requirements on the requirement-evidence engine's dashboards,
data tables, agent review screens, or multi-step product workflows. Those screens need clear
information hierarchy, evidence, accessible controls, and complete interaction states.

Explicit user instructions and BMW brand rules override generic taste defaults. In particular:

- Pure white canvas, BMW Blue `#1c69d4`, dark navy hero bands, and 700/300 typography remain.
- Inter is an approved substitute when licensed BMW Type Next Latin is unavailable.
- Rectangular buttons, cards, inputs, and chips are the default. No drop shadows.
- Light surfaces with dark hero or CTA bands are intentional BMW composition.
- Do not invent a dark theme unless requested; the supplied brand system defines a light base.
- M stripes belong only in M-model or motorsport contexts.

## Before implementation

1. Infer page kind, audience, existing brand, assets, and accessibility constraints.
2. State: "Reading this as: <page kind> for <audience>, with a <vibe> language,
   leaning toward <design system or aesthetic family>."
3. Set `DESIGN_VARIANCE`, `MOTION_INTENSITY`, and `VISUAL_DENSITY` explicitly.
   For measured BMW corporate marketing, start at 4 / 3 / 4; adapt to the brief.
4. For redesigns, audit tokens, information architecture, content, interactions, accessibility,
   analytics, and SEO before editing. Preserve routes, nav labels, form names/order, brand marks,
   and legal/consent copy unless the user authorizes changes.
5. For a specific visual reference, record concrete ratios, spacing, colors, radii, shadows,
   icon treatment, layout structure, and deliberate omissions. Mark estimates as estimates.
   Write a yes/no check for each rule and verify the composition can be rebuilt from the rules.
6. Inspect the existing stack and `package.json` before importing dependencies. Reuse the
   project's foundation; do not mix component systems or recreate an explicitly requested
   official design system by hand.

## Composition and copy

- Use the BMW spacing scale, 80px major section rhythm, 24px card padding, and 1440px container.
- Prefer purposeful alignment and real content hierarchy over decorative asymmetry.
- Marketing heroes: at most two desktop headline lines, 20 words of supporting copy,
  one primary and at most one secondary CTA. Keep CTAs visible in the initial viewport.
  Limit desktop top padding to 96px and hero text to four elements total.
- Keep desktop navigation on one line and 64px tall, with an 80px maximum.
- Use at most one section eyebrow per three marketing sections. Avoid numbered sections,
  scroll cues, version stamps, decorative status dots, atmospheric locale strips, and
  decoration text at the hero's bottom.
- Avoid repeated generic feature-card rows, empty bento cells, and three consecutive
  alternating image/text splits. Choose layouts that fit the actual content.
- Put supporting paragraphs directly below headings; avoid floating corner explainers.
- Keep marketing paragraphs short and quotes within three lines. Use disclosures, grouped
  content, or separate pages for long lists rather than dumping data into landing pages.
- Use plain, grammatical copy. Avoid forced metaphors, filler verbs, invented testimonials,
  fabricated metrics, and fake precision. Label sample data explicitly.
- Use one label per CTA intent and one verb per action throughout the product.
- Generated visible UI copy uses regular hyphens, commas, periods, or parentheses instead
  of em-dashes or en-dash separators. Preserve supplied source material as supplied.

## Assets and styling

- Use real brand assets and real component previews. Never fabricate screenshot-like
  rectangles, terminal windows, or dashboards as decorative product previews.
- For marketing surfaces needing photography, prefer suitable generated assets when tools
  are available, then verified real imagery. If assets cannot be obtained, use clearly marked
  placeholders and report the missing placements. Product workflows do not need stock imagery.
- Use real logos for genuine social proof; do not invent customers or decorative photo credits.
- Keep images free of decorative pills and labels. Reserve dimensions to prevent layout shifts.
- Use one icon family. Prefer Phosphor, HugeIcons, Radix, or Tabler; retain Lucide if already
  used by the project. Do not hand-draw SVG icon paths.
- Avoid gradient text, glows, glass panels, random accent colors, custom cursors, and ornamental
  grid lines. BMW photography and surface contrast provide depth.
- Self-host fonts with `font-display: swap`, or use `next/font` in Next.js.

## Interaction and engineering

- Provide meaningful loading, empty, error, disabled, selected, focus, and success states
  where the interaction requires them. Use layout-matched skeletons for loading.
- Put labels above form inputs, helper text alongside the field, and inline errors below.
  Placeholders are never labels. Ensure keyboard operation and visible focus.
- Check text, placeholders, focus indicators, and controls for WCAG AA contrast. Keep CTA
  labels on one desktop line and touch targets at least 48px where BMW specifies them.
- Use CSS Grid for grids and declare each multi-column layout's mobile collapse explicitly.
  Use `min-height: 100dvh` when a full-height layout is needed, rather than fixed `100vh`.
- Keep state local unless shared state is necessary. Put providers and interactive islands
  in Client Components in Next.js; static layouts can remain Server Components.
- Animate only when motion explains hierarchy, feedback, storytelling, or state changes.
  Honor reduced motion. Do not claim motion that has not been implemented.
- Use Motion values for continuous pointer/scroll values, never React state. Avoid raw scroll
  listeners. Use IntersectionObserver, CSS scroll animations, Motion, or GSAP ScrollTrigger.
- Isolate animation code in client leaves and clean up effects. Do not let animation libraries
  compete over the same elements. Keep marquees to at most one per marketing page.
- For actual GSAP pinned stacks or horizontal pans, pin at `start: "top top"` and use correct
  end distances and scrub behavior. Do not add scroll hijacks merely for decoration.
- Keep z-index layers intentional, lazy-load heavy below-the-fold code, and avoid grain filters
  on scrolling containers. Target LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, and CLS < 0.1.

## Pre-flight before delivery

Check applicable rules; mark out-of-scope items as such rather than inventing content to satisfy
them. Fix failures before delivering and report any checks that could not be run.

- Brief, mode, dials, reference rules, and BMW precedence are explicit.
- Colors, fonts, radii, spacing, and component states match `design.md`.
- Visible copy is grammatical, consistent, and free of decorative dash separators or fake data.
- Navigation, hero, CTAs, grids, and images fit desktop and mobile without overflow or clipping.
- Section layouts and eyebrow counts fit the marketing composition, with no empty filler cells.
- Assets load, previews are real, and social proof has a factual basis.
- Buttons, inputs, text, focus states, keyboard paths, and touch targets pass accessibility checks.
- Loading, empty, error, and disabled states work for relevant interactions.
- Motion is motivated, implemented, cleaned up, and disabled or simplified under reduced motion.
- Test every supported theme; do not require an invented theme merely to satisfy a generic rule.
- Run appropriate build checks and inspect the UI at desktop and mobile sizes. For marketing
  pages, run Lighthouse when a runnable browser environment is available; report measured
  results honestly instead of asserting Core Web Vitals from code inspection alone.

# Product Intelligence frontend A working, responsive PM workspace based on [`docs/idea.md`](../docs/idea.md), [`design.md`](../design.md), and the architecture docs. Uses the documented BMW blue, white, and navy palette, rectangular controls, Inter, and Phosphor icons. Live demo: [bmw-product-intelligence.vercel.app](https://bmw-product-intelligence.vercel.app). ## Run locally Use Node 24 LTS (or another version supported by Vite 7). ```bash cd frontend npm ci npm run dev ``` Open the local URL printed by Vite. Production build: ```bash npm run build npm run preview ``` ## What works - Overview with vehicle-line/market selection, baseline comparisons, editable successor targets and priorities, illustrative trend charts, and decision history. - Requirement portfolio with search, filters, explainable weighted scores, editing, reason-required approval/challenge/rejection, and filtered CSV exports with citations. - Guided research with sequential Accept/Edit/Retry/Reject gates. Rejections require a continue-with-gap or abort decision. Drafts appear only after the final review. - Evidence library with source locators, linked requirements, coverage gaps, and local document registration. Text/CSV/JSON files include a preview; binary files are not parsed. - Programme report with targets, requirements, citations, history, CSV export, and browser print/save as PDF. - Browser persistence, JSON workspace export, and an explicit reset confirmation. All seed values, excerpts, grades, and trends are **illustrative demo fixtures**, not verified BMW specifications or findings. Research does not call an AI provider, query Supabase, or search the web. Retry records steering against the same fixtures. Plans use three fixed steps, rather than the proposed live orchestrator. No automated report scheduling runs. In local development, **Evidence library → Browse backend evidence** opens the retained live Evidence browser. Run `make backend` at the repo root to serve its `/api` requests; Vite proxies them to port 8000, or `VITE_API_PROXY` when set. This mode has separate search filters and does not import live hits into the local portfolio. It is disabled in the static Vercel demo; another deployment can enable it with `VITE_LIVE_EVIDENCE=true` once `/api` is served. ### Sign-in (live mode only) Live mode needs an account on the backend. When the API answers 401 the live views show a sign-in form; the token is kept in `sessionStorage` (gone when the tab closes), sent as a Bearer header, and dropped on any 401. There is no sign-up: an administrator creates users with `python -m app.auth.manage`. The offline demo never calls the auth endpoints. ### Live mode (backend) In local development, **Research** has a **Live planner (backend)** switch and **Evidence library** has **Browse backend evidence**. Both call `/api` only (the frontend never reads the database). Live research posts your request, shows the orchestrator's real plan (which agents, why, and which are not built yet), and lets you edit the plan until an agent starts. Agents do not run yet, so there are no accept/retry controls in live mode. The live library shows every loaded source file and a coverage matrix per vehicle line and market with gaps marked. Live mode is off in the static Vercel build unless `VITE_LIVE_EVIDENCE=true` and `/api` is served. `npm run dev` listens on localhost only; use `npm run dev:lan` to expose it, which also exposes the proxied, unauthenticated API to your network. Edits and previews are stored in this browser's local storage. There is no account system, server persistence, shared workspace, immutable audit log, or restore-from-JSON UI yet. Export a backup to retain work outside this browser. See [decision 0011](../docs/decisions/0011-local-demo-frontend-and-vercel.md) for the boundary between the delivered frontend and the planned backend. ## Verification ```bash npx playwright install chromium npm test ``` Playwright exercises desktop and mobile workflows, persistence, exports, review gates, keyboard dialog focus, PDF generation, overflow, and automated axe WCAG checks on all five views. Tests require a browser environment that permits Chromium to launch. ## Structure - `src/App.tsx`: navigation, scope, dialogs, and persisted workspace state. - `src/data.ts`: typed demo fixtures, scoring, citations, CSV, and export utilities. - `src/context.tsx`: shared workspace actions. - `src/components/`: the five views, forms, and Radix-based dialog/button primitives. - `src/styles.css`: brand tokens, responsive layouts, print, and reduced-motion styles. - `src/features/evidence/`, `src/lib/api.ts`: retained backend Evidence browser and API client. - `src/index.css`, `src/shadcn-variants.css`: retained Tailwind/Base UI styling. ## Vercel Deploy **this directory** as a Vite project, with `npm run build` and output directory `dist`. `vercel.json` contains these settings. Hash navigation allows all workspace views to load and refresh from the static entry point. The Latin Inter font is hosted with the app; the frontend needs no environment variables or backend credentials. ```bash cd frontend vercel --prod ``` `.vercelignore` excludes dependencies, test artifacts, and environment files from uploads. Keep service-role/database/AI keys on a future backend; do not expose them through `VITE_*`. Deployments currently use the CLI; Git-triggered deployments are not configured. # Overview > Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (chat entry point) ## Mission Help a BMW product manager derive, justify, and prioritize customer-facing requirements for the successor of an existing vehicle line — grounded in customer feedback, BMW product/sales data, and web research — while the PM stays in control of every decision that matters. ## Scope **In scope:** customer-facing product requirements — features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment/digital services, design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging *as experienced by the customer*, variant and package offering. **Out of scope:** regulatory/homologation (safety, emissions, type approval), engineering specs/architecture/supplier topics, pricing/business-case/cost calculation (cost or effort may be used as a *rough* prioritization factor only). A finding that reads as regulatory or pricing in nature is auto-tagged and routed to a visibly separate "flagged, out of scope" bin rather than drafted into a requirement — see [`08-scaling-and-config.md`](08-scaling-and-config.md#regulatory-guardrail). ## Scope: set by the question The system is not tied to one vehicle line or market. Every line in the provided data (F70, G60/G68, G70; presumed 1 / 5 / 7 Series successors, confirm before presenting as fact) and every market (Europe, China, United States, Rest of World) is loaded, and a PM can ask in any direction: a competitor comparison, a feature gap, a market trend, a requirement derivation for one line, a question across lines. The orchestrator reads the request, picks the agents that are needed, and each agent, backed by an LLM, searches the evidence relevant to that question. Evidence is uneven (some line/market combinations have far more customer feedback than others), so sample size and confidence are shown with every result rather than hidden by narrowing the scope. ## The five stages Taken directly from BMW's own process slide — everything in this doc set is organized around it. ```mermaid flowchart LR SA["01 Situation analysis
baseline · competition ·
feedback · trends"] SC["02 Structure & context
classify · cluster ·
dedupe · contextualize"] RD["03 Requirements definition
specify · quantify ·
acceptance criteria"] PR["04 Prioritization
customer vs business,
explainable score"] DOC["05 Documentation
dossier · audit trail ·
re-embed into KB"] SA --> SC --> RD --> PR --> DOC DOC -.->|requirements tracking loop,
~quarterly over ~2 yrs| SA ``` What makes this more than a batch pipeline is **how** a PM drives it — see [`02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md): the PM starts a **chat** with a research request, an **orchestrator** plans which agents are needed, and they run one at a time. Each agent's cited answer can be pushed back on or accepted before the next agent starts, and the final result appears only after all needed agents are accepted. Not every request runs every stage. See [decision 0005](../decisions/0005-chat-entry-and-orchestrator-planned-steps.md). ## Document map See [`../README.md`](../README.md) for the full doc index. Start with [`01-agents.md`](01-agents.md) for who does what, then [`02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md`](02-orchestration-and-human-in-the-loop.md) for how a PM actually drives this. # Orchestration & human-in-the-loop: a chat that plans, then runs one agent at a time > Status: `building` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (step runner — see [decision 0015](../decisions/0015-step-runner-and-step-output-on-the-step.md); the frontend does not call it yet) This is the central mechanic of the whole system. The PM starts a **chat** with a research request. An **orchestrator** decides which agents are needed. They run **one at a time**, and each agent's answer is shown in the chat for the PM to push back on or accept **before the next agent starts**. Nothing is shown as a final result until every needed agent has been accepted. Earlier drafts gated the PM at the end only, then at every step but with a manual "Run" click per agent. The chat model keeps the per-step gate and removes the extra click: **accepting a step is what starts the next one.** ## Entry point: a chat 1. PM opens a **new chat** and types a research request, e.g. *"What would we need to stay competitive on seat comfort in the US market?"* Scope (vehicle line, market) is taken from the message or asked back in one short question if missing. 2. The **Orchestrator** reads the request and produces a **plan**: the ordered list of agents needed and why each is included (e.g. Customer Feedback → Competitor → Clustering → Requirements Drafting; Baseline and Market/Trend left out, with the reason). The plan is shown in the chat. The PM can edit it (add, remove, reorder) before the first agent starts. 3. The first agent starts. When it finishes, its answer appears as a step card in the chat. 4. The PM pushes back or accepts. On **Accept**, the orchestrator starts the next needed agent automatically, with the accepted output as context. The orchestrator may also revise the remaining plan based on what was found (e.g. add the Sales agent because a cluster needs an uptake cross-check); any change to the plan is announced in the chat. 5. After the last agent is accepted, the **final research result** is compiled and shown with citations. It is not shown earlier. Not every request needs every agent. A question that only needs feedback evidence runs two or three agents; a full requirement derivation runs the whole chain. ## How the plan is made (implemented) `POST /api/conversations/{id}/messages` stores the PM's request, asks the planner for a plan, and stores it as a `plan` message plus one `planned` step per agent. Nothing runs yet. - **The model proposes, code decides.** An OpenAI model picks agents from the catalog (`orchestration/catalog.py`) with a one-sentence reason each and extracts the scope if the request states one. Code then drops unknown agents, removes duplicates, orders by pipeline stage, and adds the prerequisites a later stage needs (Prioritization needs Drafting, Clustering and a research agent). Added prerequisites are marked as such. - **Scope is optional.** No line or market in the request means all of them (stored as `ALL`). - **Agents that are not built are still planned**, flagged `[not built yet]`, with a note in the thread, so the PM sees what the question really needs. They cannot run until they exist and can be removed from the plan. - **No hidden fallback.** If the model is unavailable the API answers 503 with the reason and stores nothing. `PLANNER=rules` selects a keyword planner for local work without a key. - **The PM can edit the plan** (`PUT /api/runs/{id}/plan`) until an agent has started. An edit is checked, never silently completed: removing a prerequisite is refused with the reason. Each edit adds a `plan_change` message. - Plans and edits are written to the audit log (`plan_created`, `plan_edited`). ## How a plan runs (implemented) `orchestration/runner.py` applies the state machine below; `orchestration/agents.py` holds one adapter per agent. | Call | Effect | |---|---| | `POST /api/runs/{id}/start` | The PM confirms the plan. The first step goes to `running` and the plan is locked | | `POST /api/steps/{id}/accept` | Step → `accepted`; the next planned step starts, or the run completes with a `final_result` message | | `POST /api/steps/{id}/retry` `{note}` | Same step back to `running` with the steering note; `attempt` + 1 | | `POST /api/steps/{id}/reject` `{note, proceed}` | Step → `rejected`; `proceed` true goes on with a coverage gap, false aborts the run | | `POST /api/steps/{id}/edit` `{summary}` | Rewrites the summary; the step stays in review | - **The agent runs after the response.** The call returns with the step `running`; the step card arrives in the thread when the agent and the Critic are done, so the client polls `GET /api/conversations/{id}`. - **The Critic is inside every run**, with one automatic retry. Claims that stay uncited are dropped and listed on the card. Synthesis steps are checked against the findings accepted earlier in the run. - **Output lives on the step** as JSON (`structured_output_refs`) and in the step card's payload. The next agent receives only the output of accepted steps. Nothing is written to the finding, cluster, requirement or score tables by a run yet. - **A failed agent** ends in `awaiting_review` with a card that says so, to retry or reject. - **An action outside its state is refused** with 409 and the reason (accepting a planned step, starting twice, acting on a finished run). - Every start, finish, accept, edit, retry and reject is an audit event on the step. ## The unit of work: a Step A `PipelineRun` (one chat request's execution, scoped to a vehicle line + market) is made of `Step`s, one per agent invocation. A step has five states: ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> planned: orchestrator adds it to the plan planned --> running: previous step accepted
(or first in plan), auto-start running --> awaiting_review: agent finishes,
Critic Agent has verified citations,
human-readable summary attached awaiting_review --> accepted: PM Accept awaiting_review --> running: PM Retry (steering note in chat) awaiting_review --> rejected: PM Reject accepted --> [*]: starts the next needed step rejected --> [*]: PM decides skip-this-agent or abort run ``` Deliberate points: - **Accept is the only trigger for the next agent.** No agent runs ahead of an unreviewed one, and there is no separate "Run" click. The gate is the review, not the launch. - **The Critic Agent sits inside `running → awaiting_review`**, not after it. A step doesn't reach the PM until every claim in its output has a live citation — see [`01-agents.md`](01-agents.md#the-critic-agent). The PM pushes back on judgment calls, not on obviously unsourced claims; those never arrive. - **One agent at a time is enforced by the database,** not only by the app: a unique index allows at most one step per run in `running` or `awaiting_review`. - **The plan can change mid-run** (orchestrator proposes, PM can veto), but a step already `accepted` is never silently re-run. ## The four actions, same verbs as everywhere else | Action | What it does | |---|---| | **Accept** | Step → `accepted`. Its `Finding`/`Cluster`/`Requirement`/`Score` output becomes real input for the next step, and the orchestrator starts that step. | | **Edit** | PM directly rewrites the human-readable summary or the underlying structured output (e.g. merges two clusters, tightens a metric) before accepting. The diff is the audit event. | | **Retry** (= Challenge, at step grain) | PM replies in the chat with a steering note ("exclude paywalled sources," "only EU respondents," "re-check that number"). Same agent, same step, re-runs with the note appended to its task. Step goes back to `running`. | | **Reject** | Step → `rejected`. PM then decides: proceed without this agent's contribution (flagged as a coverage gap on everything downstream) or abort the run. | Pushing back is a normal chat message on the step's thread, so the conversation reads as a dialogue with the system rather than a form. This reuses the exact same four verbs as the coarser requirement lifecycle ([`05-requirement-lifecycle.md`](05-requirement-lifecycle.md)) — approve/reject/edit/challenge — just applied at the grain of one agent's output instead of one finished requirement. ## Human-readable output, every time Every agent emits two things, not one: structured output for the data model, and a short `StepSummary` — plain language, always including: - what it looked at (scope, sources, filters applied) - what it found, as a short bulleted list, **each bullet carrying its citation** (source + locator: file and page/sheet/row, or URL and retrieval date) - how confident it is, and what's thin or missing - anything it flagged as out of scope (regulatory/pricing) and routed to the side bin This is what renders in the chat as the step card. The final research result is compiled from the accepted `StepSummary`s; every statement in it can only cite findings that were retrieved and accepted along the way. ## The chain (what the orchestrator chooses from) ```mermaid flowchart TD Q["PM chat request"] --> ORCH{"Orchestrator
plans needed agents"} ORCH --> A1[Baseline Agent] ORCH --> A2[Customer Feedback Agent] ORCH --> A3[Sales & Portfolio Agent] ORCH --> A4[Competitor Agent] ORCH --> A5[Market & Trend Agent] A1 & A2 & A3 & A4 & A5 -.->|only those in the plan,
one at a time, each accepted
before the next starts| SC[Clustering / Structure & context] SC --> RD[Requirements Drafting] RD --> PR[Prioritization / Scoring] PR --> DOC[Documentation — dossier,
audit events, re-embed] DOC --> FV["Final research result
(+ requirements → Draft in the normal lifecycle)"] ``` Which of these appear in a given run is the orchestrator's decision. A pure market-research question may stop after the research agents and Clustering; Drafting, Prioritization, and Documentation are added only when the request asks for requirements. When requirements are produced, each enters the normal [lifecycle](05-requirement-lifecycle.md) at `Draft` and can still be approved, edited, rejected, or challenged individually. ## Worked example — "what features would we need to stay competitive in the US market?" 1. PM starts a new chat with that question. Orchestrator replies with a plan: *Competitor → Customer Feedback (US) → Market & Trend → Clustering → Requirements Drafting → Prioritization. Skipping Baseline (no previous-generation angle asked for).* PM adds Sales & Portfolio before Clustering and confirms. 2. Competitor Agent starts. Card: *"Searched 14 competitor review/spec sources for US midsize sedans. 6 findings: 3 competitor_advantage, 2 market_trend, 1 unmet_need. 2 sources are paywalled — flagged Interpreted."* Each finding has its URL and retrieval date. 3. PM replies **Retry**: *"drop the paywalled ones, find a free equivalent or mark unverified."* Same agent re-runs. PM reviews again and clicks **Accept**. 4. Customer Feedback Agent starts automatically (US-filtered). PM accepts. Market & Trend starts, then Sales & Portfolio — each one only after the previous was accepted. 5. Clustering starts. PM **Edits** one cluster (two themes were really the same complaint), then **Accepts**. 6. Requirements Drafting starts, then Prioritization. PM reviews the score breakdown, nudges the `business_signal` weight, re-runs, **Accepts**. 7. Last agent accepted: the final research result appears in the chat, with a citation on every claim, and the draft requirements sit in the backlog at `Draft`. Every launch, retry, edit, and accept is in the audit trail (see [`07-audit-trail.md`](07-audit-trail.md)). ## Data model additions `PipelineRun` and `Step` (full schema in [`04-data-model.md`](04-data-model.md#pipelinerun--step)), plus `Conversation` and `Message` for the chat thread: a run belongs to one conversation, step cards and PM replies are messages linked to their step. ## UI shape A chat thread. The user's request, the orchestrator's plan, each step card, and the PM's pushback replies are all messages in order. A step card in `awaiting_review` shows the `StepSummary` with citations plus **Accept / Edit / Retry / Reject**; anything else is read-only history. A plan strip at the top shows which steps are planned, running, or done. It's closer to a CI pipeline with manual approval gates, driven through a chat, than to a chatbot that answers in one go — the PM is operating the system, not just chatting with it. ## Delivered frontend demo `frontend/` implements a Research view with a question composer, plan strip, cited fixture cards, and Accept / Edit / Retry / Reject actions. Only one contribution is reviewable at a time. Accept advances to the next; rejection requires an explicit coverage-gap or abort decision, including after reload. A draft appears only after the final review. This UI currently uses a fixed three-step plan and local browser state. Retry stores steering against the same illustrative evidence, and Edit records the PM's revised summary. The live mode beside it ([decision 0013](../decisions/0013-frontend-uses-only-the-backend-api.md)) shows the backend's plan and plan editing, but does not call the step runner yet, and there is no LangGraph checkpointer. The preceding sections describe the backend behavior; the [frontend guide](../../frontend/README.md) documents the implemented demo. # Repository structure: frontend and backend > Status: `building` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (PM workspace and demo/live evidence boundary; see [decision 0011](../decisions/0011-local-demo-frontend-and-vercel.md)) ```mermaid flowchart LR UI["frontend
React + shadcn/ui"] -->|"/api (JSON)"| API["backend
FastAPI"] API --> K["knowledge layer
retrieval tools"] API --> O["orchestration
step state machine"] O --> AG["agents"] AG --> K K --> DB[("Supabase Postgres
+ pgvector")] ING["ingest
loaders, parsers"] --> DB AG -->|findings| DB K -.->|embeddings, answers| OAI["OpenAI API"] ``` The browser never talks to the database or to OpenAI. The only door is the backend's `/api`. ## Layout ``` backend/ pyproject.toml dependencies, pytest config; `pip install -e "backend[dev]"` app/ main.py FastAPI app (CORS, routers) config.py repo-root .env and data/ paths, settings; no secrets in logs auth/ password hashing, users and sessions, the admin script (`python -m app.auth.manage`) api/ HTTP layer: health, evidence search / counts / cite / filters, response schemas knowledge/ retrieval tools every agent uses; each hit carries a citation agents/ LLM-backed agents (Market & Trend today) orchestration/ agent catalog, planner, chat and plan persistence, step state machine ingest/ loaders and parsers for the provided PDFs and Excel files tests/ pytest; no database or OpenAI key needed frontend/ Gabriel's PM workspace (npm, Vite + React + TypeScript), see frontend/README.md src/App.tsx, components/ the five views over local demo data (fixtures, browser storage) src/features/research/ live research: conversations, the planner's real plan, plan editing (calls /api) src/features/library/ live evidence library: loaded sources and coverage matrix (calls /api) src/features/evidence/ live evidence search with exact counts (calls /api) src/components/ui/ shadcn/ui components used by the live views, restyled with BMW tokens src/lib/api.ts the only place the frontend talks to the backend; src/types/api.ts mirrors the schemas supabase/migrations/ schema, applied in filename order docs/ architecture, decisions, requirements skills/ agent skills (database setup, scripts) data/ provided BMW files, gitignored Makefile .env.example common tasks and the environment template (one .env at the repo root) ``` ## Rules - **Dependencies point inward.** `api` calls `knowledge` and `orchestration`; `agents` call `knowledge`; `knowledge` talks to the database. `api` never writes SQL, and nothing imports from `api`. - **Python imports are `app.`**, scripts run as `python -m app..`, so paths never depend on the working directory. - **One source for response shapes:** `backend/app/api/schemas.py`, mirrored by `frontend/src/types/api.ts`. Change both together. - **Every API result that states a fact carries a citation** (file, location, verbatim quote). - **The frontend never touches the database.** Every live view calls `/api`; all SQL is in the backend. The demo views use fixtures, labelled as such, and the static Vercel build has no live mode. - **UI follows `design.md`:** BMW tokens, rectangular components, no shadows, Inter 300/700 as the approved substitute font, no dark theme. Components keep labels above fields and show loading, empty and error states. - **Tests:** `make test` for the backend (the API tests replace the knowledge tools with fakes). The frontend is checked by `make build` (type-check and bundle), `make lint`, and `npm test` from `frontend/` (desktop/mobile Playwright workflows and automated accessibility checks). ## API today | Endpoint | Returns | |---|---| | `POST /api/auth/login` | public: email and password in, a session token out; every failure reads the same, five wrong passwords lock the account for 15 minutes | | `GET /api/auth/me`, `POST /api/auth/logout` | who am I; revoke this session | | `GET /api/health` | database and OpenAI-key status (never connection details) | | `GET /api/evidence/search?q=&source=feedback\|docs&line=&market=&domain=&polarity=&powertrain=&k=` | cited hits, hybrid vector and keyword search | | `GET /api/evidence/stats?group_by=&line=&market=...` | exact counts and their total | | `GET /api/evidence/filters` | the values the UI offers as filters | | `GET /api/evidence/{kind}/{id}` | the citation for one stored row | | `GET /api/sources` | every loaded source file with what was extracted from it (comments, passages, options, study cells, sales rows) | | `GET /api/evidence/coverage` | comments, study cells and 2025 sales per vehicle line and market, so gaps are visible | | `GET /api/agents` | the agent catalog in pipeline order and which agents exist yet | | `GET, POST /api/conversations` | list, or create (optionally with a first request) | | `GET, PATCH /api/conversations/{id}` | the thread (messages and runs with steps), or rename / archive | | `POST /api/conversations/{id}/messages` | a PM request: the orchestrator plans and stores `planned` steps | | `PUT /api/runs/{id}/plan` | the PM edits the plan before any agent starts | | `POST /api/runs/{id}/start` | the PM confirms the plan; the first agent starts in the background | | `POST /api/steps/{id}/accept`, `retry`, `reject`, `edit` | the PM's four actions on a step in review; accept starts the next agent | Everything except `/api/health` and `/api/auth/login` needs `Authorization: Bearer `; without it the answer is a uniform 401 and no database connection is opened. Bad parameters give 422, unknown rows 404, and an unreachable database 503 with no internals in the message. Interactive docs are served at `/docs`. ## Not built yet - Starting the plan: accepting the plan, running the first step, and the PM actions on a step card (accept, edit, retry, reject). The chat API and the planner exist; the agents behind the steps and the runner do not. - The Requirements, Overview and Reports views still show local demo data; they need requirements and findings in the database first. - A Docker setup and CI. ## Frontend delivery The active UI is the five-view PM workspace documented in [the frontend guide](../../frontend/README.md). build:

## Overview

BMW's corporate site carries a far more **measured, corporate-automotive** interface than its motorsport-bombastic cousin BMW M. The atmosphere is light: `{colors.canvas}` (#ffffff) is the base surface, `{colors.surface-card}` (#fafafa) carries the soft-grey card plates, and dark navy `{colors.surface-dark}` (#1a2129) appears only inside hero bands — one per page, framing the lead model render.

Type runs BMW's licensed **BMW Type Next Latin** at two weights: heavy 700 (display + button + nav) and Light 300 (body + secondary copy). That contrast — heavy display next to thin paragraph — is the editorial signature, channeling the brand's "European-engineered" voice. Weight 500 is deliberately absent; weight 400 only appears on caption and nav-link in neutral utility contexts.

The brand action color, **BMW corporate blue** (`{colors.primary}` — #1c69d4), works alone across every primary CTA — buttons are **rectangular, 0px corner**, with white type. The site rotates a blue-button + dark-navy-hero combination across page rhythm. The M tricolor stripe (`{colors.m-blue-light}` → `{colors.m-blue-dark}` → `{colors.m-red}`) only appears in motorsport contexts and as M-model badges/dividers — never in the corporate site's main language.

The configuration and reservation flows add a dealer-side inventory UI on top of the same system — filter chips, model cards, price tables — but typography and color stay identical; only density goes up.

**Key Characteristics:**
- Light `{colors.canvas}` is the base surface; dark navy `{colors.surface-dark}` appears only inside hero bands — page rhythm relies on contrast.
- BMW corporate blue (`{colors.primary}` — #1c69d4) acts as the single primary action color.
- BMW Type Next Latin: weight 700 display against weight 300 body is the signature.
- Buttons are **rectangular, 0px radius** — corporate dialect, distinct from M's sportier radii.
- Model cards run as 4-up or 5-up grids with no hairline border or only minimal border — just white plate + photo + title.
- Photography (model renders) sits in environment, no shadow — depth comes entirely from color-block contrast.
- M tricolor stripe appears only in M-model contexts — not part of the corporate language.
- Section rhythm holds at `{spacing.section}` (80px) for every major band.

## Colors

### Brand & Accent
- **BMW Blue (Primary)** (`{colors.primary}` — #1c69d4): The single brand action color. All primary CTAs, "Learn More" link prefixes (blue text), nav-link active state. Press shifts to `{colors.primary-active}` (#0653b6).
- **M Blue Light** (`{colors.m-blue-light}` — #0066b1) + **M Blue Dark** (`{colors.m-blue-dark}` — #1c69d4) + **M Red** (`{colors.m-red}` — #e22718): The M tricolor stripe — appears on the corporate site only on M-model pages and the "M" badge. Never as CTA colors.

### Surface
- **Canvas** (`{colors.canvas}` — #ffffff): The default page surface.
- **Surface Soft** (`{colors.surface-soft}` — #f7f7f7): Soft grey for the footer and sub-navigation bands.
- **Surface Card** (`{colors.surface-card}` — #fafafa): The light plate behind a model card's photo block.
- **Surface Strong** (`{colors.surface-strong}` — #ebebeb): A slightly heavier grey used as a section divider.
- **Surface Dark** (`{colors.surface-dark}` — #1a2129): Dark navy for hero bands and large dark CTAs. Not pure black — carries a warm undertone.
- **Surface Dark Elevated** (`{colors.surface-dark-elevated}` — #262e38): One step lighter, used for nested cards on top of the dark hero.

### Hairlines
- **Hairline** (`{colors.hairline}` — #e6e6e6): The 1px divider — input outline, configurator card outline, table separator.
- **Hairline Strong** (`{colors.hairline-strong}` — #cccccc): A more visible 1px outline — disabled secondary buttons, emphasized table border.

### Text
- **Ink** (`{colors.ink}` — #262626): All display and primary text. Not pure black — soft against photography.
- **Body** (`{colors.body}` — #3c3c3c): Default running text.
- **Body Strong** (`{colors.body-strong}` — #1a1a1a): Emphasized paragraphs and lead text.
- **Muted** (`{colors.muted}` — #6b6b6b): Footer links, breadcrumbs, captions.
- **Muted Soft** (`{colors.muted-soft}` — #9a9a9a): Disabled text, fine-print legal.

### Semantic
- **Success** (`{colors.success}` — #22c55e): Confirmation messages and "available" indicators.
- **Warning** (`{colors.warning}` — #f59e0b): Warning callouts.
- **Error** (`{colors.error}` — #dc2626): Validation errors.

## Typography

### Font Family
The system runs **BMW Type Next Latin** in two cuts: regular (display + UI labels) and **BMW Type Next Latin Light** (body + secondary copy). Fallback stack: `system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif`.

The display/body split is functional:
- BMW Type Next Latin (700) → display headlines, button labels, nav links
- BMW Type Next Latin Light (300) → paragraphs, descriptive copy
- BMW Type Next Latin (400) → caption, neutral nav-link contexts

This three-way split mirrors BMW M's — corporate and the M sub-brand share the same typographic DNA; only the weight/size ratios differ.

### Hierarchy

| Token | Size | Weight | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{typography.display-xl}` | 64px | 700 | 1.05 | 0 | Hero h1 ("iX3", model name) |
| `{typography.display-lg}` | 48px | 700 | 1.1 | 0 | Section heads |
| `{typography.display-md}` | 32px | 700 | 1.15 | 0 | Sub-section heads |
| `{typography.display-sm}` | 24px | 700 | 1.25 | 0 | CTA-band headlines |
| `{typography.title-lg}` | 20px | 700 | 1.3 | 0 | Card group titles |
| `{typography.title-md}` | 18px | 700 | 1.4 | 0 | Model card title, intro paragraphs |
| `{typography.title-sm}` | 16px | 700 | 1.4 | 0 | Inventory card title, list label |
| `{typography.body-md}` | 16px | 300 (Light) | 1.55 | 0 | Default body — BMW Type Next Latin Light |
| `{typography.body-sm}` | 14px | 300 (Light) | 1.55 | 0 | Footer body, fine-print |
| `{typography.caption}` | 12px | 400 | 1.4 | 0.5px | Photo captions, meta |
| `{typography.label-uppercase}` | 13px | 700 | 1.3 | 1.5px | "LEARN MORE" inline links, category tabs |
| `{typography.button}` | 14px | 700 | 1.0 | 0.5px | Standard CTA button label |
| `{typography.nav-link}` | 14px | 400 | 1.4 | 0.3px | Top-nav menu items |

### Principles
- The **700/300 contrast** is the editorial signature. Weight 500 is absent from the system.
- **No negative letter-spacing** — BMW Type Next Latin works on a wide body, so tracking stays at default. Apple/Cal.com-style tightening reads off-brand here.
- **UPPERCASE inline links** — "LEARN MORE"-style CTAs run uppercase with 1.5px tracking. The "machined precision" voice.
- **Weight 400 lives in a narrow lane** — only caption and nav-link, both neutral utility roles.

### Note on Font Substitutes
BMW Type Next Latin is a licensed BMW typeface. Open-source alternatives:
- **Inter** (variable) — close match at weight 700/300. Leave letter-spacing at 0.0em.
- **Saira Condensed** — for a slightly more compressed BMW Type feel.

## Layout

### Spacing System
- **Base unit:** 8px.
- **Tokens:** `{spacing.xxs}` 4px · `{spacing.xs}` 8px · `{spacing.sm}` 12px · `{spacing.md}` 16px · `{spacing.lg}` 24px · `{spacing.xl}` 32px · `{spacing.xxl}` 48px · `{spacing.section}` 80px.
- **Section padding:** `{spacing.section}` (80px) for every major editorial band.
- **Card internal padding:** `{spacing.lg}` (24px) for model and feature cards.

### Grid & Container
- **Max content width:** ~1440px center-aligned.
- **Editorial body:** A single 12-column grid.
- **Model card grids:** 4-up or 5-up at desktop, 2-up at tablet, 1-up on mobile.
- **Configurator inventory grids:** 3-up filter row + 4-up vehicle cards, dense layout.

### Whitespace Philosophy
BMW's whitespace strategy is tighter than BMW M's motorsport-aerated grenadier — the corporate side is more utility-driven. Section rhythm is 80px (not M's 96px). Card padding is 24px (not M's 32px). The page is denser, more dealership-functional.

## Elevation & Depth

| Level | Treatment | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Flat | No shadow, no border | Body, top nav, footer, hero bands |
| Soft hairline | 1px `{colors.hairline}` border | Configurator option tile, table divider |
| Card surface | `{colors.surface-card}` background — no shadow | Model card photo plate |
| Photographic | Edge-to-edge photography | Hero band, model renders |

The system never uses a drop shadow. Depth comes entirely from (a) color-block contrast (light canvas vs dark hero) and (b) photographic subject + lighting.

### Decorative Depth
- **`m-stripe-divider`** — a 4px-tall horizontal tricolor stripe (`{colors.m-blue-light}` → `{colors.m-blue-dark}` → `{colors.m-red}`). Only in M-model contexts, motorsport badges, or as an M-related section divider. Not part of the main corporate flow.
- **Photographic depth** — full-bleed vehicle photography (lighting + subject) does the work chrome would otherwise do.

## Shapes

### Border Radius Scale

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `{rounded.none}` | 0px | Every button, card, input, configurator chip — the dominant radius |
| `{rounded.xs}` | 2px | Very small badges, very rare |
| `{rounded.sm}` | 4px | Small inline button (rare) |
| `{rounded.md}` | 8px | Mobile-only collapse cards (rare) |
| `{rounded.lg}` | 12px | Very rare — modal/dialog corners |
| `{rounded.pill}` | 9999px | Filter chips in some contexts (rare) |
| `{rounded.full}` | 9999px / 50% | Avatar, circular icon button |

The radius hierarchy is binary: **rectangular for everything, circular only for icon buttons.** A clear departure from the soft-cornered SaaS dialect of Apple or Cal.com — closer to BMW corporate-automotive's "engineered precision" voice.

### Photography Geometry
- Hero photography is full-bleed at 16:9 or 21:9 cinematic ratio.
- Model card photos sit at 16:10, edge-to-edge with `{rounded.none}` corners.
- Configurator vehicle renders sit on a white studio background, full silhouette visible.

## Data model additions

`PipelineRun` and `Step` (full schema in [`04-data-model.md`](04-data-model.md#pipelinerun--step)),
plus `Conversation` and `Message` for the chat thread: a run belongs to one conversation, step

## UI shape

A chat thread. The user's request, the orchestrator's plan, each step card, and the PM's pushback
replies are all messages in order. A step card in `awaiting_review` shows the `StepSummary` with
citations plus **Accept / Edit / Retry / Reject**; anything else is read-only history. A plan strip
at the top shows which steps are planned, running, or done. It's closer to a CI pipeline with
manual approval gates, driven through a chat, than to a chatbot that answers in one go — the PM is
operating the system, not just chatting with it.

decision, including after reload. A draft appears only after the final review.

This UI currently uses a fixed three-step plan and local browser state. Retry stores steering

## Rules

- **Dependencies point inward.** `api` calls `knowledge` and `orchestration`; `agents` call `knowledge`;
  `knowledge` talks to the database. `api` never writes SQL, and nothing imports from `api`.
- **Python imports are `app.<package>`**, scripts run as `python -m app.<package>.<module>`, so paths
  never depend on the working directory.
- **One source for response shapes:** `backend/app/api/schemas.py`, mirrored by `frontend/src/types/api.ts`.
  Change both together.
- **Every API result that states a fact carries a citation** (file, location, verbatim quote).
- **The frontend never touches the database.** Every live view calls `/api`; all SQL is in the backend. The demo
  views use fixtures, labelled as such, and the static Vercel build has no live mode.
- **UI follows `design.md`:** BMW tokens, rectangular components, no shadows, Inter 300/700 as the
  approved substitute font, no dark theme. Components keep labels above fields and show loading, empty and
  error states.
- **Tests:** `make test` for the backend (the API tests replace the knowledge tools with fakes). The
  frontend is checked by `make build` (type-check and bundle), `make lint`, and `npm test`
  from `frontend/` (desktop/mobile Playwright workflows and automated accessibility checks).

## API today

| Endpoint | Returns |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/auth/login` | public: email and password in, a session token out; every failure reads the same, five wrong passwords lock the account for 15 minutes |
| `GET /api/auth/me`, `POST /api/auth/logout` | who am I; revoke this session |
| `GET /api/health` | database and OpenAI-key status (never connection details) |
| `GET /api/evidence/search?q=&source=feedback\|docs&line=&market=&domain=&polarity=&powertrain=&k=` | cited hits, hybrid vector and keyword search |
| `GET /api/evidence/stats?group_by=&line=&market=...` | exact counts and their total |
| `GET /api/evidence/filters` | the values the UI offers as filters |
| `GET /api/evidence/{kind}/{id}` | the citation for one stored row |
| `GET /api/sources` | every loaded source file with what was extracted from it (comments, passages, options, study cells, sales rows) |
| `GET /api/evidence/coverage` | comments, study cells and 2025 sales per vehicle line and market, so gaps are visible |
| `GET /api/agents` | the agent catalog in pipeline order and which agents exist yet |
| `GET, POST /api/conversations` | list, or create (optionally with a first request) |
| `GET, PATCH /api/conversations/{id}` | the thread (messages and runs with steps), or rename / archive |
| `POST /api/conversations/{id}/messages` | a PM request: the orchestrator plans and stores `planned` steps |
| `PUT /api/runs/{id}/plan` | the PM edits the plan before any agent starts |
| `POST /api/runs/{id}/start` | the PM confirms the plan; the first agent starts in the background |
| `POST /api/steps/{id}/accept`, `retry`, `reject`, `edit` | the PM's four actions on a step in review; accept starts the next agent |

Everything except `/api/health` and `/api/auth/login` needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; without it the answer is a
uniform 401 and no database connection is opened. Bad parameters give 422, unknown rows 404, and an unreachable database 503 with no internals in the
message. Interactive docs are served at `/docs`.

# UI design guidelines

Project-specific adaptation of the supplied `design-taste-frontend` guidance.
Read alongside [`../design.md`](../design.md), which defines the BMW design system.

## Scope and precedence

Use BMW tokens for every generated UI. Apply the marketing-page guidance below to landing
pages, portfolios, editorial pages, and redesigns. Do not impose marketing hero, photography,
section variety, or short-copy requirements on the requirement-evidence engine's dashboards,
data tables, agent review screens, or multi-step product workflows. Those screens need clear
information hierarchy, evidence, accessible controls, and complete interaction states.

Explicit user instructions and BMW brand rules override generic taste defaults. In particular:

- Pure white canvas, BMW Blue `#1c69d4`, dark navy hero bands, and 700/300 typography remain.
- Inter is an approved substitute when licensed BMW Type Next Latin is unavailable.
- Rectangular buttons, cards, inputs, and chips are the default. No drop shadows.
- Light surfaces with dark hero or CTA bands are intentional BMW composition.
- Do not invent a dark theme unless requested; the supplied brand system defines a light base.
- M stripes belong only in M-model or motorsport contexts.

## Before implementation

1. Infer page kind, audience, existing brand, assets, and accessibility constraints.
2. State: "Reading this as: <page kind> for <audience>, with a <vibe> language,
   leaning toward <design system or aesthetic family>."
3. Set `DESIGN_VARIANCE`, `MOTION_INTENSITY`, and `VISUAL_DENSITY` explicitly.
   For measured BMW corporate marketing, start at 4 / 3 / 4; adapt to the brief.
4. For redesigns, audit tokens, information architecture, content, interactions, accessibility,
   analytics, and SEO before editing. Preserve routes, nav labels, form names/order, brand marks,
   and legal/consent copy unless the user authorizes changes.
5. For a specific visual reference, record concrete ratios, spacing, colors, radii, shadows,
   icon treatment, layout structure, and deliberate omissions. Mark estimates as estimates.
   Write a yes/no check for each rule and verify the composition can be rebuilt from the rules.
6. Inspect the existing stack and `package.json` before importing dependencies. Reuse the
   project's foundation; do not mix component systems or recreate an explicitly requested
   official design system by hand.

## Composition and copy

- Use the BMW spacing scale, 80px major section rhythm, 24px card padding, and 1440px container.
- Prefer purposeful alignment and real content hierarchy over decorative asymmetry.
- Marketing heroes: at most two desktop headline lines, 20 words of supporting copy,
  one primary and at most one secondary CTA. Keep CTAs visible in the initial viewport.
  Limit desktop top padding to 96px and hero text to four elements total.
- Keep desktop navigation on one line and 64px tall, with an 80px maximum.
- Use at most one section eyebrow per three marketing sections. Avoid numbered sections,
  scroll cues, version stamps, decorative status dots, atmospheric locale strips, and
  decoration text at the hero's bottom.
- Avoid repeated generic feature-card rows, empty bento cells, and three consecutive
  alternating image/text splits. Choose layouts that fit the actual content.
- Put supporting paragraphs directly below headings; avoid floating corner explainers.
- Keep marketing paragraphs short and quotes within three lines. Use disclosures, grouped
  content, or separate pages for long lists rather than dumping data into landing pages.
- Use plain, grammatical copy. Avoid forced metaphors, filler verbs, invented testimonials,
  fabricated metrics, and fake precision. Label sample data explicitly.
- Use one label per CTA intent and one verb per action throughout the product.
- Generated visible UI copy uses regular hyphens, commas, periods, or parentheses instead
  of em-dashes or en-dash separators. Preserve supplied source material as supplied.

## Assets and styling

- Use real brand assets and real component previews. Never fabricate screenshot-like
  rectangles, terminal windows, or dashboards as decorative product previews.
- For marketing surfaces needing photography, prefer suitable generated assets when tools
  are available, then verified real imagery. If assets cannot be obtained, use clearly marked
  placeholders and report the missing placements. Product workflows do not need stock imagery.
- Use real logos for genuine social proof; do not invent customers or decorative photo credits.
- Keep images free of decorative pills and labels. Reserve dimensions to prevent layout shifts.
- Use one icon family. Prefer Phosphor, HugeIcons, Radix, or Tabler; retain Lucide if already
  used by the project. Do not hand-draw SVG icon paths.
- Avoid gradient text, glows, glass panels, random accent colors, custom cursors, and ornamental
  grid lines. BMW photography and surface contrast provide depth.
- Self-host fonts with `font-display: swap`, or use `next/font` in Next.js.

## Interaction and engineering

- Provide meaningful loading, empty, error, disabled, selected, focus, and success states
  where the interaction requires them. Use layout-matched skeletons for loading.
- Put labels above form inputs, helper text alongside the field, and inline errors below.
  Placeholders are never labels. Ensure keyboard operation and visible focus.
- Check text, placeholders, focus indicators, and controls for WCAG AA contrast. Keep CTA
  labels on one desktop line and touch targets at least 48px where BMW specifies them.
- Use CSS Grid for grids and declare each multi-column layout's mobile collapse explicitly.
  Use `min-height: 100dvh` when a full-height layout is needed, rather than fixed `100vh`.
- Keep state local unless shared state is necessary. Put providers and interactive islands
  in Client Components in Next.js; static layouts can remain Server Components.
- Animate only when motion explains hierarchy, feedback, storytelling, or state changes.
  Honor reduced motion. Do not claim motion that has not been implemented.
- Use Motion values for continuous pointer/scroll values, never React state. Avoid raw scroll
  listeners. Use IntersectionObserver, CSS scroll animations, Motion, or GSAP ScrollTrigger.
- Isolate animation code in client leaves and clean up effects. Do not let animation libraries
  compete over the same elements. Keep marquees to at most one per marketing page.
- For actual GSAP pinned stacks or horizontal pans, pin at `start: "top top"` and use correct
  end distances and scrub behavior. Do not add scroll hijacks merely for decoration.
- Keep z-index layers intentional, lazy-load heavy below-the-fold code, and avoid grain filters
  on scrolling containers. Target LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, and CLS < 0.1.

## Pre-flight before delivery

Check applicable rules; mark out-of-scope items as such rather than inventing content to satisfy
them. Fix failures before delivering and report any checks that could not be run.

- Brief, mode, dials, reference rules, and BMW precedence are explicit.
- Colors, fonts, radii, spacing, and component states match `design.md`.
- Visible copy is grammatical, consistent, and free of decorative dash separators or fake data.
- Navigation, hero, CTAs, grids, and images fit desktop and mobile without overflow or clipping.
- Section layouts and eyebrow counts fit the marketing composition, with no empty filler cells.
- Assets load, previews are real, and social proof has a factual basis.
- Buttons, inputs, text, focus states, keyboard paths, and touch targets pass accessibility checks.
- Loading, empty, error, and disabled states work for relevant interactions.
- Motion is motivated, implemented, cleaned up, and disabled or simplified under reduced motion.
- Test every supported theme; do not require an invented theme merely to satisfy a generic rule.
- Run appropriate build checks and inspect the UI at desktop and mobile sizes. For marketing
  pages, run Lighthouse when a runnable browser environment is available; report measured
  results honestly instead of asserting Core Web Vitals from code inspection alone.
