## Overview

BMW's corporate site carries a far more **measured, corporate-automotive** interface than its motorsport-bombastic cousin BMW M. The atmosphere is light: `{colors.canvas}` (#ffffff) is the base surface, `{colors.surface-card}` (#fafafa) carries the soft-grey card plates, and dark navy `{colors.surface-dark}` (#1a2129) appears only inside hero bands — one per page, framing the lead model render.

Type runs BMW's licensed **BMW Type Next Latin** at two weights: heavy 700 (display + button + nav) and Light 300 (body + secondary copy). That contrast — heavy display next to thin paragraph — is the editorial signature, channeling the brand's "European-engineered" voice. Weight 500 is deliberately absent; weight 400 only appears on caption and nav-link in neutral utility contexts.

The brand action color, **BMW corporate blue** (`{colors.primary}` — #1c69d4), works alone across every primary CTA — buttons are **rectangular, 0px corner**, with white type. The site rotates a blue-button + dark-navy-hero combination across page rhythm. The M tricolor stripe (`{colors.m-blue-light}` → `{colors.m-blue-dark}` → `{colors.m-red}`) only appears in motorsport contexts and as M-model badges/dividers — never in the corporate site's main language.

The configuration and reservation flows add a dealer-side inventory UI on top of the same system — filter chips, model cards, price tables — but typography and color stay identical; only density goes up.

**Key Characteristics:**
- Light `{colors.canvas}` is the base surface; dark navy `{colors.surface-dark}` appears only inside hero bands — page rhythm relies on contrast.
- BMW corporate blue (`{colors.primary}` — #1c69d4) acts as the single primary action color.
- BMW Type Next Latin: weight 700 display against weight 300 body is the signature.
- Buttons are **rectangular, 0px radius** — corporate dialect, distinct from M's sportier radii.
- Model cards run as 4-up or 5-up grids with no hairline border or only minimal border — just white plate + photo + title.
- Photography (model renders) sits in environment, no shadow — depth comes entirely from color-block contrast.
- M tricolor stripe appears only in M-model contexts — not part of the corporate language.
- Section rhythm holds at `{spacing.section}` (80px) for every major band.

## Colors

### Brand & Accent
- **BMW Blue (Primary)** (`{colors.primary}` — #1c69d4): The single brand action color. All primary CTAs, "Learn More" link prefixes (blue text), nav-link active state. Press shifts to `{colors.primary-active}` (#0653b6).
- **M Blue Light** (`{colors.m-blue-light}` — #0066b1) + **M Blue Dark** (`{colors.m-blue-dark}` — #1c69d4) + **M Red** (`{colors.m-red}` — #e22718): The M tricolor stripe — appears on the corporate site only on M-model pages and the "M" badge. Never as CTA colors.

### Surface
- **Canvas** (`{colors.canvas}` — #ffffff): The default page surface.
- **Surface Soft** (`{colors.surface-soft}` — #f7f7f7): Soft grey for the footer and sub-navigation bands.
- **Surface Card** (`{colors.surface-card}` — #fafafa): The light plate behind a model card's photo block.
- **Surface Strong** (`{colors.surface-strong}` — #ebebeb): A slightly heavier grey used as a section divider.
- **Surface Dark** (`{colors.surface-dark}` — #1a2129): Dark navy for hero bands and large dark CTAs. Not pure black — carries a warm undertone.
- **Surface Dark Elevated** (`{colors.surface-dark-elevated}` — #262e38): One step lighter, used for nested cards on top of the dark hero.

### Hairlines
- **Hairline** (`{colors.hairline}` — #e6e6e6): The 1px divider — input outline, configurator card outline, table separator.
- **Hairline Strong** (`{colors.hairline-strong}` — #cccccc): A more visible 1px outline — disabled secondary bu…1401 tokens truncated… chrome would otherwise do.

## Shapes

### Border Radius Scale

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `{rounded.none}` | 0px | Every button, card, input, configurator chip — the dominant radius |
| `{rounded.xs}` | 2px | Very small badges, very rare |
| `{rounded.sm}` | 4px | Small inline button (rare) |
| `{rounded.md}` | 8px | Mobile-only collapse cards (rare) |
| `{rounded.lg}` | 12px | Very rare — modal/dialog corners |
| `{rounded.pill}` | 9999px | Filter chips in some contexts (rare) |
| `{rounded.full}` | 9999px / 50% | Avatar, circular icon button |

The radius hierarchy is binary: **rectangular for everything, circular only for icon buttons.** A clear departure from the soft-cornered SaaS dialect of Apple or Cal.com — closer to BMW corporate-automotive's "engineered precision" voice.

### Photography Geometry
- Hero photography is full-bleed at 16:9 or 21:9 cinematic ratio.
- Model card photos sit at 16:10, edge-to-edge with `{rounded.none}` corners.
- Configurator vehicle renders sit on a white studio background, full silhouette visible.

## Components

### Top Navigation

**`top-nav`** — A white sticky nav bar pinned to the top of the page. 64px tall, `{colors.canvas}` background. Left: BMW circular badge logo; center: primary horizontal menu (Models, Next Generation, Pre-Owned, Dealers, Test Drive); right: cart icon, language picker, profile. Menu items render in `{typography.nav-link}` (14px / 400 / 0.3px tracking).

### Buttons

**`button-primary`** — The signature primary CTA. Background `{colors.primary}` (BMW Blue #1c69d4), text `{colors.on-primary}`, type `{typography.button}` (BMW Type Next Latin 14px / 700 / 0.5px tracking), padding 14px × 32px, height 48px, rounded `{rounded.none}` (0px — rectangular). Press state: `button-primary-active` shifts to `{colors.primary-active}`.

**`button-secondary`** — A white button with a hairline outline. Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, 1px `{colors.hairline-strong}` border, same padding + height + radius.

**`button-secondary-on-dark`** — Used over a dark hero band. Background transparent, text `{colors.on-dark}`, 1px `{colors.on-dark}` border, same rectangular shape.

**`button-text-link`** — An inline UPPERCASE letter-spaced link. No background, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.label-uppercase}` (13px / 700 / 1.5px tracking). Reads as "LEARN MORE", terminated by a `›` chevron.

**`text-link`** — An inline link inside body copy. `{colors.ink}` text, no underline by default; underlines per context.

### Cards & Containers

**`hero-band-dark`** — Full-width dark navy hero. Background `{colors.surface-dark}`, text `{colors.on-dark}`, vertical padding `{spacing.section}` (80px). Centered: model name in `{typography.display-xl}` (64px / 700) + sub-headline + vehicle render (right-aligned or below). A single `{component.button-primary}` (blue) or `{component.button-secondary-on-dark}`.

**`hero-photo-band`** — A light-canvas model showcase band. Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`. The vehicle render takes the wide area; right or below, a headline + two link CTAs + sub-tagline.

**`model-card`** — Used in 4-up or 5-up model card grids on the homepage ("BMW iX3", "BMW iX", "BMW 5 Series"). Background `{colors.canvas}`, rounded `{rounded.none}`, padding `{spacing.lg}` (24px). Contents: model render at the top (`{component.model-card-photo}` on `{colors.surface-card}`), model name in `{typography.title-md}` (18px / 700) below, a one-line tagline in `{typography.body-sm}` (14px / 300), and a `{component.button-text-link}` ("LEARN MORE ›").

**`model-card-photo`** — The card's photo plate. Background `{colors.surface-card}` (#fafafa — soft grey), rounded `{rounded.none}`, vehicle render in full silhouette. Zero padding — the photo runs edge-to-edge.

**`feature-photo-card`** — A feature/lifestyle card. Background `{colors.canvas}`, padding `{spacing.lg}`. 16:9 photo at the top, `{typography.title-md}` headline + body excerpt below.

**`spec-cell`** — A technical spec cell (model detail page). Transparent background, separated by hairline dividers. Value on top (`{typography.display-sm}` 24px / 700), label below (`{typography.label-uppercase}`).

### Inventory & Configurator

**`inventory-card`** — One card per vehicle on the dealer inventory page. Background `{colors.canvas}`, padding `{spacing.md}` (16px), rounded `{rounded.none}`. Vehicle photo on top, model + variant name + price + "View" link below.

**`filter-chip`** + **`filter-chip-active`** — Inventory filter chips (model, year, price range). Inactive: background `{colors.canvas}`, 1px `{colors.hairline-strong}` border, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.caption}`. Active: background `{colors.ink}`, text `{colors.on-dark}`. Padding 8px × 14px, radius `{rounded.none}`.

**`configurator-option-tile`** + **`configurator-option-tile-selected`** — Configurator selection cell (color, wheels, upholstery). Inactive: background `{colors.canvas}`, 1px hairline. Selected: 2px `{colors.primary}` border. Padding 16px × 24px, radius `{rounded.none}`.

### Inputs & Forms

**`text-input`** — Standard text input. Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.body-md}`, rounded `{rounded.none}` (0px), padding 14px × 16px, height 48px, 1px hairline border. On focus, the border thickens to ink.

**`cookie-consent-card`** — Cookie banner. Background `{colors.canvas}`, 1px hairline, padding `{spacing.lg}` (24px), `{typography.body-sm}` (14px / 300 — Light even in legal copy).

### Tabs / Tags

**`category-tab`** + **`category-tab-active`** — Category sub-nav. Inactive: transparent + `{colors.muted}` UPPERCASE label. Active: transparent + `{colors.ink}` UPPERCASE label + 2px ink underline. 12px vertical padding, no horizontal radius.

### Brand Signature

**`m-stripe-divider`** — A 4px-tall horizontal tricolor stripe (`{colors.m-blue-light}` → `{colors.m-blue-dark}` → `{colors.m-red}`). Only in M-model contexts, motorsport badges, or as an M-related section divider. Absent from the corporate main flow; on M-model detail pages and the M Performance badge it plays an inline divider role.

### CTA / Footer

**`cta-band-photo`** — A pre-footer "Discover the New iX3"-style band. Background `{colors.surface-dark}` with a full-bleed vehicle photo. Centered headline in `{typography.display-md}` (32px / 700) + a single `{component.button-secondary-on-dark}`. 80px padding.

**`footer`** — The closing soft-grey footer. Background `{colors.surface-soft}` (#f7f7f7 — not pure white — soft grey), text `{colors.body}`. A 4-column link list: Models / Services / Dealers / About. Vertical padding 64px. Below, a copyright line in `{typography.body-sm}` with `{colors.muted}`.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do
- Sit every page on `{colors.canvas}` (pure white); reserve `{colors.surface-dark}` for hero bands only.
- Pair primary CTAs with `{colors.primary}` (BMW Blue) + `{colors.on-primary}` white text + `{rounded.none}` 0px corners — the corporate signature.
- Set display headlines in BMW Type Next Latin 700 and body in Light 300. The contrast is non-negotiable.
- Use UPPERCASE letter-spaced links like "LEARN MORE" as inline CTAs.
- Place the model card photo on `{colors.surface-card}` with the title beneath — the standard BMW corporate pattern.
- Hold section rhythm at `{spacing.section}` (80px) — tighter than BMW M's 96px.
- Reserve the M tricolor stripe for M-model contexts and motorsport dividers.

### Don't
- Don't add a brand color other than blue — BMW Blue is the only primary action color.
- Don't use pill or rounded buttons — `{rounded.none}` (0px) rectangular IS the brand button.
- Don't drop display weight to 500 — the system uses 700 / 400 / 300; 500 is absent.
- Don't bold body type — Light 300 is the BMW corporate editorial voice.
- Don't add drop shadows to cards — depth comes from photo + color-block contrast.
- Don't repeat the same surface mode across two consecutive bands — light → dark hero → light → light feature → dark CTA → light footer rotation is required.
- Don't use the M tricolor stripe as a CTA fill — divider/accent role only.
- Don't mix languages in a single page — UI language must stay consistent.

## Responsive Behavior

### Breakpoints

| Name | Width | Key Changes |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile | < 768px | Hamburger nav; hero h1 64→40px; model card grid 1-up; configurator filter chips 2-up; footer 4 col → 1 col |
| Tablet | 768–1024px | Top nav narrows, secondary menu hides under "More"; model card 2-up; inventory 2-up |
| Desktop | 1024–1440px | Full top-nav; 4-up or 5-up model card grid; inventory 3-up; full configurator UI |
| Wide | > 1440px | Same as desktop, content fixed at 1440px; gutters absorb the rest |

### Touch Targets
- `{component.button-primary}` minimum 48 × 48px — above WCAG AAA (44 × 44).
- `{component.text-input}` height 48px.
- Category tabs run with 12px vertical padding, giving an effective tap area > 44px.

### Collapsing Strategy
- The top nav collapses to a hamburger below 768px; the menu opens as a full-screen sheet.
- The hero band's internal layout drops to a single column.
- Model card grid 4-up/5-up → 2-up → 1-up.
- The configurator filter chip row scrolls horizontally on mobile.
- The M tricolor stripe stays at 4px height across every breakpoint.

### Image Behavior
- Model renders scale at every breakpoint while preserving native aspect ratios.
- Hero photography may shift to a more vertical crop on mobile (art direction).
- Inventory vehicle photos may move from 16:9 to 4:3 on mobile.

## Iteration Guide

1. Focus on a single component. Reference its YAML key directly (`{component.model-card}`, `{component.button-primary}`).
2. New components default to `{rounded.none}` (0px). Use `{rounded.full}` only for circular icon buttons.
3. Variants (`-active`, `-disabled`, `-selected`) live as separate entries inside the `components:` block.
4. `{token.refs}` everywhere — never inline hex.
5. Hover state is never documented. Only Default and Active/Pressed states.
6. Display headlines stay BMW Type Next Latin 700; body stays Light 300; the trio is fixed.
7. Keep UI strings in a single language — match the locale of the page.

## Known Gaps

- BMW Type Next Latin is licensed to BMW and not published as a public web font; Inter at weights 700/300 is documented as the substitute.
- Animation and transition timings (configurator color swap, model card hover-reveal) are out of scope here.
- Form validation states beyond `{component.text-input}` focus were not extracted — error/success states would need a dedicated form page.
- The dealer inventory sub-domain shares typography and color with the main corporate site; only UI density rises (filters, tables, prices).
- A cookie consent overlay can occlude part of the hero — the lead hero band content may not be fully captured.
- The M tricolor stripe appears infrequently on this corporate site; full motorsport context lives on the BMW M site.
# UI design guidelines

Project-specific adaptation of the supplied `design-taste-frontend` guidance.
Read alongside [`../design.md`](../design.md), which defines the BMW design system.

## Scope and precedence

Use BMW tokens for every generated UI. Apply the marketing-page guidance below to landing
pages, portfolios, editorial pages, and redesigns. Do not impose marketing hero, photography,
section variety, or short-copy requirements on the requirement-evidence engine's dashboards,
data tables, agent review screens, or multi-step product workflows. Those screens need clear
information hierarchy, evidence, accessible controls, and complete interaction states.

Explicit user instructions and BMW brand rules override generic taste defaults. In particular:

- Pure white canvas, BMW Blue `#1c69d4`, dark navy hero bands, and 700/300 typography remain.
- Inter is an approved substitute when licensed BMW Type Next Latin is unavailable.
- Rectangular buttons, cards, inputs, and chips are the default. No drop shadows.
- Light surfaces with dark hero or CTA bands are intentional BMW composition.
- Do not invent a dark theme unless requested; the supplied brand system defines a light base.
- M stripes belong only in M-model or motorsport contexts.

## Before implementation

1. Infer page kind, audience, existing brand, assets, and accessibility constraints.
2. State: "Reading this as: <page kind> for <audience>, with a <vibe> language,
   leaning toward <design system or aesthetic family>."
3. Set `DESIGN_VARIANCE`, `MOTION_INTENSITY`, and `VISUAL_DENSITY` explicitly.
   For measured BMW corporate marketing, start at 4 / 3 / 4; adapt to the brief.
4. For redesigns, audit tokens, information architecture, content, interactions, accessibility,
   analytics, and SEO before editing. Preserve routes, nav labels, form names/order, brand marks,
   and legal/consent copy unless the user authorizes changes.
5. For a specific visual reference, record concrete ratios, spacing, colors, radii, shadows,
   icon treatment, layout structure, and deliberate omissions. Mark estimates as estimates.
   Write a yes/no check for each rule and verify the composition can be rebuilt from the rules.
6. Inspect the existing stack and `package.json` before importing dependencies. Reuse the
   project's foundation; do not mix component systems or recreate an explicitly requested
   official design system by hand.

## Composition and copy

- Use the BMW spacing scale, 80px major section rhythm, 24px card padding, and 1440px container.
- Prefer purposeful alignment and real content hierarchy over decorative asymmetry.
- Marketing heroes: at most two desktop headline lines, 20 words of supporting copy,
  one primary and at most one secondary CTA. Keep CTAs visible in the initial viewport.
  Limit desktop top padding to 96px and hero text to four elements total.
- Keep desktop navigation on one line and 64px tall, with an 80px maximum.
- Use at most one section eyebrow per three marketing sections. Avoid numbered sections,
  scroll cues, version stamps, decorative status dots, atmospheric locale strips, and
  decoration text at the hero's bottom.
- Avoid repeated generic feature-card rows, empty bento cells, and three consecutive
  alternating image/text splits. Choose layouts that fit the actual content.
- Put supporting paragraphs directly below headings; avoid floating corner explainers.
- Keep marketing paragraphs short and quotes within three lines. Use disclosures, grouped
  content, or separate pages for long lists rather than dumping data into landing pages.
- Use plain, grammatical copy. Avoid forced metaphors, filler verbs, invented testimonials,
  fabricated metrics, and fake precision. Label sample data explicitly.
- Use one label per CTA intent and one verb per action throughout the product.
- Generated visible UI copy uses regular hyphens, commas, periods, or parentheses instead
  of em-dashes or en-dash separators. Preserve supplied source material as supplied.

## Assets and styling

- Use real brand assets and real component previews. Never fabricate screenshot-like
  rectangles, terminal windows, or dashboards as decorative product previews.
- For marketing surfaces needing photography, prefer suitable generated assets when tools
  are available, then verified real imagery. If assets cannot be obtained, use clearly marked
  placeholders and report the missing placements. Product workflows do not need stock imagery.
- Use real logos for genuine social proof; do not invent customers or decorative photo credits.
- Keep images free of decorative pills and labels. Reserve dimensions to prevent layout shifts.
- Use one icon family. Prefer Phosphor, HugeIcons, Radix, or Tabler; retain Lucide if already
  used by the project. Do not hand-draw SVG icon paths.
- Avoid gradient text, glows, glass panels, random accent colors, custom cursors, and ornamental
  grid lines. BMW photography and surface contrast provide depth.
- Self-host fonts with `font-display: swap`, or use `next/font` in Next.js.

## Interaction and engineering

- Provide meaningful loading, empty, error, disabled, selected, focus, and success states
  where the interaction requires them. Use layout-matched skeletons for loading.
- Put labels above form inputs, helper text alongside the field, and inline errors below.
  Placeholders are never labels. Ensure keyboard operation and visible focus.
- Check text, placeholders, focus indicators, and controls for WCAG AA contrast. Keep CTA
  labels on one desktop line and touch targets at least 48px where BMW specifies them.
- Use CSS Grid for grids and declare each multi-column layout's mobile collapse explicitly.
  Use `min-height: 100dvh` when a full-height layout is needed, rather than fixed `100vh`.
- Keep state local unless shared state is necessary. Put providers and interactive islands
  in Client Components in Next.js; static layouts can remain Server Components.
- Animate only when motion explains hierarchy, feedback, storytelling, or state changes.
  Honor reduced motion. Do not claim motion that has not been implemented.
- Use Motion values for continuous pointer/scroll values, never React state. Avoid raw scroll
  listeners. Use IntersectionObserver, CSS scroll animations, Motion, or GSAP ScrollTrigger.
- Isolate animation code in client leaves and clean up effects. Do not let animation libraries
  compete over the same elements. Keep marquees to at most one per marketing page.
- For actual GSAP pinned stacks or horizontal pans, pin at `start: "top top"` and use correct
  end distances and scrub behavior. Do not add scroll hijacks merely for decoration.
- Keep z-index layers intentional, lazy-load heavy below-the-fold code, and avoid grain filters
  on scrolling containers. Target LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, and CLS < 0.1.

## Pre-flight before delivery

Check applicable rules; mark out-of-scope items as such rather than inventing content to satisfy
them. Fix failures before delivering and report any checks that could not be run.

- Brief, mode, dials, reference rules, and BMW precedence are explicit.
- Colors, fonts, radii, spacing, and component states match `design.md`.
- Visible copy is grammatical, consistent, and free of decorative dash separators or fake data.
- Navigation, hero, CTAs, grids, and images fit desktop and mobile without overflow or clipping.
- Section layouts and eyebrow counts fit the marketing composition, with no empty filler cells.
- Assets load, previews are real, and social proof has a factual basis.
- Buttons, inputs, text, focus states, keyboard paths, and touch targets pass accessibility checks.
- Loading, empty, error, and disabled states work for relevant interactions.
- Motion is motivated, implemented, cleaned up, and disabled or simplified under reduced motion.
- Test every supported theme; do not require an invented theme merely to satisfy a generic rule.
- Run appropriate build checks and inspect the UI at desktop and mobile sizes. For marketing
  pages, run Lighthouse when a runnable browser environment is available; report measured
  results honestly instead of asserting Core Web Vitals from code inspection alone.

item.aggregated_output: # Agent rules Project: BMW hackathon requirement-evidence engine. Architecture docs live in `docs/` (start at `docs/README.md`); those `.md` files are the source of truth. ## Repository layout - `backend/` FastAPI app and Python package `app` (`api/`, `knowledge/`, `agents/`, `ingest/`, `orchestration/`), tests in `backend/tests/`. Run with `make backend`, test with `make test`. - `frontend/` Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui. Run with `make frontend`, build with `make build`. - `supabase/migrations/` SQL migrations, `docs/` architecture and decisions, `skills/` agent skills, `data/` provided BMW files (gitignored). One `.env` at the repo root. See `docs/architecture/12-repo-structure.md`. - The frontend talks to the backend only through `/api`; it never touches the database directly. - Put new Python code under `backend/app/`, import it as `app.`, and run scripts as `python -m app..`. ## UI design - Before generating or changing UI, read `design.md`, `docs/ui-design-guidelines.md` and `docs/frontend-style-guide.md`. Find and add components with the shadcn MCP (or `npx shadcn@latest`), use the `frontend-design` skill, and review the result in screenshots with Playwright at desktop and mobile sizes before delivering. - Use the BMW tokens and component rules in `design.md` for all UI. - Apply the anti-slop workflow in `docs/ui-design-guidelines.md`. BMW's explicit brand rules take precedence over generic aesthetic defaults, including white surfaces and the Inter fallback. Shape and elevation follow decision 0021 (rounded components, soft shadows), not the rectangular default. ## Database - Postgres on Supabase (pgvector). To connect, set up a machine or teammate, check the state, apply migrations, load data or fix a connection error, read `skills/database-setup/SKILL.md` first. - Check the connection with `python skills/database-setup/scripts/check_db.py --openai`. - Never print, log, commit or paste secrets (`SUPABASE_DB_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, passwords, keys). - **Every API route needs a signed-in user by default.** New routers go into the `protected` router in `backend/app/api/__init__.py`. Only `/api/health` and `/api/auth/login` are public; a test checks every route, so do not add to the public list without a decision record. Never print or commit tokens or passwords; users are created by a human with `python -m app.auth.manage`. - Agents read evidence through `backend/app/knowledge/tools.py`, not hand-written SQL. ## Pushing 1. **Only push when the user asks.** Never push on your own initiative. 2. **Always squash before pushing.** Collapse all local work since the branch diverged from `main` into a single commit (`git reset --soft $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)` then commit, or `git merge-base` + `git rebase -i` equivalent without interactive flags). One push = one commit. 3. **Commit message:** imperative subject line, then a short body listing what changed and why. Mention any `docs/decisions/` entry added or changed. 4. **Never push to `main` directly** unless the user explicitly says so; work on a branch and open a PR. Never force-push `main`. Force-pushing your own feature branch after a squash is fine (`--force-with-lease`). 5. **Never commit** `data/` (BMW-provided files), `.env`, or any secret. Check `git status` before committing; if any of those show up as staged, stop and fix `.gitignore`. ## Docs and design decisions - When a design decision changes, edit the relevant `docs/architecture/*.md` in place, bump its `Last updated` date, and add a dated entry in `docs/decisions/` (see `docs/decisions/README.md`). Do this in the same commit as the code change that motivated it. ## Syncing to Supabase after a push After a successful push, sync the project record to Supabase. Any agent can do this from a shell: 1. Run `python skills/database-setup/scripts/sync_docs.py` from a checkout of the pushed commit. It upserts `docs/decisions/*.md` into `design_decisions` and `docs/architecture/*.md` into `architecture_docs` with the commit sha. (Supabase MCP tools may be used instead if available.) 2. Schema changes go through `python skills/database-setup/scripts/apply_migration.py ` (try `--dry-run` first), never ad-hoc DDL, and the migration file is committed in the same squashed commit. 3. Check the current state with `python skills/database-setup/scripts/check_db.py` before changing schema, and review the Supabase advisors after DDL. 4. Report what was synced in the final message. If a sync step fails or is skipped, say so explicitly. Do not claim the sync is done. The git repo is the source of truth; Supabase is a mirror. Never edit docs only in Supabase. # Frontend style guide How the frontend is built and changed. Read with [`../design.md`](../design.md) (brand tokens), [`ui-design-guidelines.md`](ui-design-guidelines.md) (anti-slop workflow) and [decision 0021](decisions/0021-rounded-chat-first-frontend.md) (rounded, chat-first look). Where they disagree, 0021 wins on shape and elevation; `design.md` wins on colour and type. ## Stack Vite, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui (style `base-nova`, **Base UI** primitives, not Radix), lucide icons. Components live in `frontend/src/components/ui/`, features in `src/features//`, shared chrome in `src/components/layout/`. The UI talks only to `/api` through `src/lib/api.ts`. ## Look and feel | Aspect | Rule | |---|---| | Colour | White canvas, `canvas-tint` (#f6f7f9) behind white cards. BMW Blue (`primary`) is the only action colour. Semantic colours only for state. No gradients, glows, glass. | | Type | Inter Variable. Body 400, headings 600, no negative tracking beyond `-0.01em` on headings. | | Shape | `--radius` 0.75rem. Cards `rounded-2xl`, inputs and buttons `rounded-xl`, chat bubbles and composer `rounded-3xl`, chips and avatars pills. | | Elevation | `shadow-xs` on cards, `shadow-sm` on primary buttons, `shadow-md` on the composer and sign-in panel only. | | Icons | lucide only, `size-4` inline, `size-5` in headings. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden`. Never hand-draw SVG. | | Spacing | 4px scale. Page gutters `px-4 sm:px-8`. Chat column `max-w-3xl`, pages `max-w-6xl`. | | Motion | Only `.rise` (new messages) and `.typing-dot`. Both are disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`. | | Copy | Plain sentences, no em or en dashes, one verb per action ("Send", "Search", "Sign out"). No invented data: examples are labelled as examples. | ## Layout patterns - **Shell:** `App.tsx` holds a 288px sidebar (`components/layout/Sidebar.tsx`) and the main column. Below `md` the sidebar is a `Sheet`. - **Chat view:** `h-dvh` column, scrolling thread, composer pinned at the bottom. The empty state centres the composer. - **Content pages:** wrap in `PageShell` (icon, title, one-line description, scrolling body on `canvas-tint`). - **State shared across views** (chat list, open chat) lives in `features/research/chat-store.tsx`. Keep other state local. - Every async view has loading (layout-matched `Skeleton`), empty, error (`role="alert"`) and success states. ## Building a UI change: the workflow 1. **Read** `design.md`, `ui-design-guidelines.md` and this file. Skim the nearest existing feature for conventions. 2. **Pick components with the shadcn MCP** before writing markup: - `search_items_in_registries` / `list_items_in_registries` to find a component or block, - `view_items_in_registries` and `get_item_examples_from_registries` to read source and usage, - `get_add_command_for_items` for the install command, then run `npx shadcn@latest add @shadcn/`. - If the MCP is not connected, the CLI does the same (`npx shadcn@latest search`, `view`, `add`). Do not recreate a shadcn component by hand. 3. **Use the design skills.** Invoke the `frontend-design` skill for hierarchy and typography choices and the `vercel:shadcn` skill for composition and theming. State the reading ("Reading this as: for ...") from the guidelines. 4. **Check what the CLI generated** (see pitfalls). Adjust the new file to the tokens above instead of overriding it at every call site. 5. **Iterate visually with Playwright.** Start the dev server, mock `/api` with `page.route` (reuse `tests/helpers.ts`: `withSession`, `json`), screenshot desktop (1440x1000) and mobile (iPhone 13) to the scratchpad, look at the images, fix, repeat. Do at least: empty state, populated state, working/loading, error, and the mobile menu. Delete throwaway screenshot specs afterwards. 6. **Verify:** `npm run build` (type-check), `npx oxlint`, `npx playwright test` (desktop and mobile, includes an axe WCAG AA check on each page). 7. **Docs:** a changed design rule needs an edit here or in `design.md` plus a dated entry in `docs/decisions/`, in the same commit. ## Accessibility (enforced by the axe checks) - Visible `

# Scaling & configuration

> Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (chat wording)

Nothing about G60 or "Europe" is hardcoded. Every `PipelineRun` (one per chat request) takes a config:
`{vehicle_line, market, generation_baseline}`, read from the PM's message or asked back by the
orchestrator if missing. Swapping to the 1 Series in China is a config
change, not a rewrite.

## Domain taxonomy is config, not code

Exterior / Interior / Powertrain / Driver Assistance / Infotainment / Comfort & Space / Usability
/ Variant & Package / Range & Charging / Safety (flagged out of scope) — stored as an editable `Ontology` store (see
[`04-data-model.md`](04-data-model.md#ontology)), not a hardcoded enum, so a future BEV-only line
can extend it without a code change.

## New source = one adapter

Every ingestion agent implements the same `Source → Finding[]` interface (see
[`03-ingestion.md`](03-ingestion.md)). A new feedback export, a new web source, a new internal
system plugs in without touching clustering, drafting, or scoring.

## Markets compose, they don't collapse

A requirement can carry per-market sub-scores and a market-fit flag ("fits EU, doesn't fit China")
rather than forcing one global priority — this is the direct answer to the PM pain point raised
about balancing requirements across regions with different climate, usage, and culture.

## Regulatory guardrail

Findings that read as safety/emissions/type-approval or pricing/business-case in nature are
auto-tagged by the Clustering/Ontology Agent and routed to a visibly separate "flagged, out of
scope" bin — never drafted into a customer requirement. Keeps the demo honestly inside the brief's
boundary instead of silently drifting into engineering or regulatory territory.
# Prioritization

> Status: `building` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (implemented, see [decision 0014](../decisions/0014-all-roster-agents-implemented.md))

A composite score the PM can see decomposed, re-weight, and override — never a black-box rank. It
balances what BMW's own slide calls "Customer" against "Business," plus the brief's allowance for
a rough cost/effort factor.

```
score = w_c · customer_relevance + w_b · business_signal + w_s · strategic_fit − w_e · effort_proxy
```

Default weights (PM-editable per program): `w_c = 0.40`, `w_b = 0.25`, `w_s = 0.15`, `w_e = 0.20`.
Not tuned to any real dataset — a defensible starting point, nothing more.

| Component | Derived from |
|---|---|
| `customer_relevance` | Finding prevalence normalized by sample size, sentiment severity, cross-source corroboration count, market-weighted when several markets are in scope |
| `business_signal` | Uptake % of the related option in `sales_volumes.xlsx`, plus competitor-coverage gap from the Competitor Agent. A sellability proxy, not a cost model — pricing/business-case math is out of scope |
| `strategic_fit` | Continuity with the previous-generation baseline (Baseline Agent) and the PM's stated themes for this program |
| `effort_proxy` | Coarse Low/Med/High heuristic (new hardware > software/UX change). Deliberately rough, always PM-editable |
| `confidence` | Evidence-level mix + source independence count. Shown as a **separate badge**, never folded silently into rank, so "high potential, thin evidence" stays visually distinct from "confidently low priority" |

Every stored `Score` keeps the weight vector used, each raw component value, who/what computed it,
a timestamp, and a one-line generated rationale — see
[`04-data-model.md`](04-data-model.md#score) — and is versioned, so re-scoring after new evidence
never erases what a priority call used to look like.

## Implementation

[`backend/app/agents/prioritization_agent.py`](../../backend/app/agents/prioritization_agent.py) computes the
formula in code, with no model. The sub-weights that turn findings into each component are constants at the top
of the module and are a starting point like the weights above. Effort maps to low 0.05, medium 0.50, high 0.95.
A missing input counts as zero, lowers confidence by 0.10 and is listed on the score. The provided data has no
option take rate, so `business_signal` uses the share of variants where the option is standard, flagged as a
proxy. The tier is proposed on the score and never written to the requirement.

## Worked example

`R-2031` — *Fast-response seat ventilation*, built around BMW's own slide example.

- **Score:** 0.49 / 1.00 → Tier 2 (should-have). Tiers: ≥0.65 must-have, 0.40–0.65 should-have,
  <0.40 watch-list.
- **customer_relevance 0.78** — two independent BMW-internal findings (a verbatim complaint and a
  customer-study item scored 2.9/5, n=340, EU) corroborate a comfort gap.
- **business_signal 0.41** — moderate option-uptake signal; one competitor review notes a faster
  rival response time (review-estimated, not lab-verified — flagged as an assumption).
- **strategic_fit 0.60** — aligns with the program's stated comfort-parity theme.
- **effort_proxy low** — software/calibration change, not new hardware.
- **confidence 0.65** — moderate; EU-only sample so far, no lab-verified benchmark yet.

Rationale (agent-generated): *"Two independent BMW-internal sources plus one competitor review
corroborate a comfort gap; moderate business signal from option uptake; low estimated effort —
lands mid-tier pending a lab-verified response-time benchmark."*

Full linked findings, assumptions, and its audit trail are in
[`07-audit-trail.md`](07-audit-trail.md#worked-example-r-2031).
# Product Intelligence frontend

A minimal React UI over the backend API. It holds no demo data: everything on screen comes from `/api`.
Design rules are in [`design.md`](../design.md) and [`docs/ui-design-guidelines.md`](../docs/ui-design-guidelines.md);
the decision is [0017](../docs/decisions/0017-minimal-live-only-frontend.md).

## Run locally

Node 24 LTS (or another version supported by Vite 7). From the repo root, `make dev` runs backend and frontend; or:

```bash
cd frontend
npm ci
npm run dev      # /api is proxied to http://localhost:8000, or VITE_API_PROXY
npm run build    # type-check and production build
npm test         # Playwright, desktop and mobile, with axe checks; every API call is mocked
```

## Views

- **Sign in**: shown whenever there is no valid session. There is no sign-up; an administrator creates users with
  `python -m app.auth.manage`. The token is kept in `sessionStorage`, sent as a Bearer header and dropped on any 401.
- **Research**: send a request and watch the orchestrator work. It chooses agents itself, reads each result and
  decides whether to call another ([decision 0018](../docs/decisions/0018-orchestrator-decides-in-an-agentic-loop.md)).
  The thread shows each decision with its reason, each agent's cited result and the final result. Nothing to approve.
  It refreshes while a run is in progress; one request runs at a time.
- **Evidence**: search customer feedback and catalog text with filters; every hit shows its citation. Exact counts by group.
- **Sources**: coverage per vehicle line and market with gaps marked, and the loaded source files.

## Structure

- `src/App.tsx`: sign-in gate, top bar, hash navigation.
- `src/features/{auth,research,evidence,library}/`: the views.
- `src/lib/api.ts`, `src/types/api.ts`: the API client and its types (mirrors `backend/app/api/schemas.py`).
- `src/components/ui/`, `src/index.css`: shadcn components and the BMW tokens.

## Deploying

Serve the `dist` build from an origin that also serves `/api` (see `vercel.json` for the Vercel settings). Keep
database and AI keys on the backend; never expose them through `VITE_*`.

"""Retrieval tools over the knowledge layer. Every hit carries a Citation (file + locator + quote)
resolved from the stored row, so an agent can only cite what it actually retrieved.

Semantic + keyword search:  search_feedback, search_docs
Exact lookups:              get_options, get_sales, get_study
Counting:                   feedback_stats, feedback_rows
Citations:                  cite

Needs OPENAI_API_KEY and SUPABASE_DB_URL in .env.   Demo:  python -m app.knowledge.tools
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from functools import lru_cache

import psycopg
from app.config import load_env
from openai import OpenAI
from psycopg.rows import dict_row

load_env()
EMBED_MODEL = "text-embedding-3-small"
QUOTE_CHARS = 300


@dataclass
class Citation:
    kind: str          # feedback | pdf_text | option | study | sales
    id: str
    file: str
    locator: str       # e.g. "sheet Feedback_Explorer, row 4642 (G60-3695)" or "page 14"
    quote: str

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f'{self.file}, {self.locator}: "{self.quote}"'


@dataclass
class Hit:
    citation: Citation
    text: str
    meta: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    score: float | None = None


_connection: psycopg.Connection | None = None


def _conn() -> psycopg.Connection:
    """One shared autocommit connection, reopened if it was closed or dropped.
    psycopg serialises calls on a connection, so the API threadpool can share it; switch to a pool
    (psycopg_pool) if request volume ever makes that the bottleneck."""
    global _connection
    if _connection is None or _connection.closed or _connection.broken:
        _connection = psycopg.connect(os.environ["SUPABASE_DB_URL"], autocommit=True, row_factory=dict_row)
    return _connection


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def _openai() -> OpenAI:
    return OpenAI()


def _embed(text: str) -> str:
    v = _openai().embeddings.create(model=EMBED_MODEL, input=text).data[0].embedding
    return "[" + ",".join(f"{x:.7f}" for x in v) + "]"


def _quote(text: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(text.split())[:QUOTE_CHARS]


def resolve_domain(name: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Top-level ontology domain id from its key ('usability') or label ('Comfort & Space')."""
    if not name:
        return None
    row = _conn().execute(
        "select id from public.ontology where kind='domain' and parent_id is null "
        "and (key = %s or label ilike %s) limit 1", (name.lower(), name + "%")).fetchone()
    if not row:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown domain: {name}")
    return str(row["id"])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- semantic + keyword search

def search_feedback(query: str, *, line: str | None = None, market: str | None = None,
                    domain: str | None = None, polarity: str | None = None,
                    powertrain: str | None = None, k: int = 10) -> list[Hit]:
    """Customer comments, hybrid vector + keyword search, filtered by normalized fields.
    line: F70|G60|G68|G70, market: EU|CN|US|RoW, polarity: positive|negative|request,
    powertrain: ICE|PHEV|BEV, domain: top-level ontology domain key or label."""
    rows = _conn().execute(
        "select * from public.search_feedback(%s::extensions.vector, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s::uuid, %s, %s)",
        (_embed(query), query, k, line, market, resolve_domain(domain), polarity, powertrain)).fetchall()
    return [Hit(
        Citation("feedback", str(r["id"]), r["file"], f"sheet {r['sheet']}, row {r['row_no']} ({r['ext_id']})",
                 _quote(r["comment"])),
        r["comment"],
        {k_: r[k_] for k_ in ("vehicle_line", "market_code", "country", "powertrain", "feedback_type",
                              "polarity", "domain", "similarity")},
        r["score"]) for r in rows]


def search_docs(query: str, *, line: str | None = None, k: int = 8) -> list[Hit]:
    """Catalog PDF text (German), hybrid search. Cite by file + page."""
    rows = _conn().execute(
        "select * from public.search_docs(%s::extensions.vector, %s, %s, %s)",
        (_embed(query), query, k, line)).fetchall()
    return [Hit(
        Citation("pdf_text", str(r["id"]), r["file"], f"page {r['page']}", _quote(r["content"])),
        r["content"],
        {"title": r["title"], "vehicle_line": r["vehicle_line"], "heading": r["heading"],
         "similarity": r["similarity"]},
        r["score"]) for r in rows]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- exact lookups

def get_options(*, line: str | None = None, variant: str | None = None, status: str | None = None,
                text: str | None = None, limit: int = 25) -> list[Hit]:
    """Equipment options with per-variant availability. status: standard|optional.
    text matches the option name/description (case-insensitive, German)."""
    rows = _conn().execute(
        "select o.id, o.vehicle_line, o.code, o.name, o.description, o.section, o.page, s.uri, "
        "  json_agg(json_build_object('variant', v.name, 'powertrain', v.powertrain, 'status', a.status, "
        "    'price_gross', a.price_gross, 'condition', a.condition) order by a.entry_no, v.name) as availability "
        "from public.option o join public.source s on s.id = o.source_id "
        "join public.option_availability a on a.option_id = o.id join public.model_variant v on v.id = a.variant_id "
        "where (%(line)s::text is null or o.vehicle_line = %(line)s) "
        "  and (%(text)s::text is null or o.name ilike '%%' || %(text)s || '%%' or o.description ilike '%%' || %(text)s || '%%') "
        "  and (%(variant)s::text is null or v.name = %(variant)s) "
        "  and (%(status)s::text is null or a.status = %(status)s) "
        "group by o.id, s.uri order by o.vehicle_line, o.page, o.code limit %(limit)s",
        {"line": line, "variant": variant, "status": status, "text": text, "limit": limit}).fetchall()
    return [Hit(
        Citation("option", str(r["id"]), r["uri"], f"page {r['page']}, SA {r['code']}",
                 _quote(r["name"] + (" — " + r["description"] if r["description"] else ""))),
        r["name"], {"vehicle_line": r["vehicle_line"], "code": r["code"], "section": r["section"],
                    "availability": r["availability"]}) for r in rows]


def get_sales(*, line: str | None = None, market: str | None = None, year: int | None = None) -> list[Hit]:
    """Sales volumes by line, market and year (2030 is a forecast). Market codes EU|CN|US|RoW."""
    rows = _conn().execute(
        "select v.id, v.vehicle_line, v.market, v.market_code, v.year, v.volume, v.is_forecast, v.sheet, v.row_no, s.uri "
        "from public.sales_volume v join public.source s on s.id = v.source_id "
        "where (%(l)s::text is null or v.vehicle_line = %(l)s) and (%(m)s::text is null or v.market_code = %(m)s) "
        "and (%(y)s::int is null or v.year = %(y)s) order by v.vehicle_line, v.market_code, v.year",
        {"l": line, "m": market, "y": year}).fetchall()
    return [Hit(
        Citation("sales", str(r["id"]), r["uri"], f"sheet {r['sheet']}, row {r['row_no']}",
                 f"{r['vehicle_line']} {r['market']} {r['year']}: {r['volume']} units"
                 + (" (forecast)" if r["is_forecast"] else "")),
        f"{r['volume']}", {k_: r[k_] for k_ in ("vehicle_line", "market_code", "year", "volume", "is_forecast")})
        for r in rows]


def get_study(*, line: str | None = None, market: str | None = None, question: str | None = None,
              limit: int = 60) -> list[Hit]:
    """Customer-study results: mean ratings (EU/CN) or answer shares (US). question matches by substring."""
    rows = _conn().execute(
        "select r.id, r.vehicle_line, r.market_code, r.model, r.question, r.metric, r.answer_option, r.value, "
        "r.sheet, r.cell_ref, s.uri from public.study_response r join public.source s on s.id = r.source_id "
        "where (%(l)s::text is null or r.vehicle_line = %(l)s) and (%(m)s::text is null or r.market_code = %(m)s) "
        "and (%(q)s::text is null or r.question ilike '%%' || %(q)s || '%%') "
        "order by r.question, r.market_code, r.model, r.answer_option limit %(n)s",
        {"l": line, "m": market, "q": question, "n": limit}).fetchall()
    return [Hit(
        Citation("study", str(r["id"]), r["uri"], f"sheet {r['sheet']}, cell {r['cell_ref']}",
                 f"{r['question']} | {r['model']} | {(r['answer_option'] + ' ') if r['answer_option'] else ''}"
                 f"{r['metric']} = {float(r['value']):.3f}"),
        r["question"], {k_: r[k_] for k_ in ("vehicle_line", "market_code", "model", "metric", "answer_option")}
        | {"value": float(r["value"])}) for r in rows]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- counting

_GROUPS = {"vehicle_line": "f.vehicle_line", "market_code": "f.market_code", "country": "f.country",
           "powertrain": "f.powertrain", "polarity": "f.polarity", "feedback_type": "f.feedback_type",
           "domain": "coalesce(p.label, 'unmapped')"}


def feedback_stats(group_by: str, *, line: str | None = None, market: str | None = None,
                   domain: str | None = None, polarity: str | None = None,
                   powertrain: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Comment counts grouped by one field, under optional filters. Counts are exact (SQL), not sampled."""
    if group_by not in _GROUPS:
        raise ValueError(f"group_by must be one of {sorted(_GROUPS)}")
    return _conn().execute(
        f"select {_GROUPS[group_by]} as key, count(*) as n from public.feedback_raw f "
        "left join public.ontology c on c.id = f.domain_id left join public.ontology p on p.id = coalesce(c.parent_id, c.id) "
        "where (%(l)s::text is null or f.vehicle_line = %(l)s) and (%(m)s::text is null or f.market_code = %(m)s) "
        "and (%(d)s::uuid is null or p.id = %(d)s) and (%(po)s::text is null or f.polarity = %(po)s) "
        "and (%(pt)s::text is null or f.powertrain = %(pt)s) group by 1 order by 2 desc",
        {"l": line, "m": market, "d": resolve_domain(domain), "po": polarity, "pt": powertrain}).fetchall()


def feedback_rows(*, line: str | None = None, market: str | None = None, domain: str | None = None,
                  polarity: str | None = None, powertrain: str | None = None, limit: int = 20,
                  offset: int = 0) -> list[Hit]:
    """The concrete comments behind a count, for linking a finding to its evidence rows."""
    rows = _conn().execute(
        "select f.id, f.comment, f.sheet, f.row_no, f.ext_id, f.vehicle_line, f.market_code, f.polarity, "
        "f.powertrain, s.uri from public.feedback_raw f join public.source s on s.id = f.source_id "
        "left join public.ontology c on c.id = f.domain_id left join public.ontology p on p.id = coalesce(c.parent_id, c.id) "
        "where (%(l)s::text is null or f.vehicle_line = %(l)s) and (%(m)s::text is null or f.market_code = %(m)s) "
        "and (%(d)s::uuid is null or p.id = %(d)s) and (%(po)s::text is null or f.polarity = %(po)s) "
        "and (%(pt)s::text is null or f.powertrain = %(pt)s) order by f.row_no limit %(n)s offset %(o)s",
        {"l": line, "m": market, "d": resolve_domain(domain), "po": polarity, "pt": powertrain,
         "n": limit, "o": offset}).fetchall()
    return [Hit(Citation("feedback", str(r["id"]), r["uri"], f"sheet {r['sheet']}, row {r['row_no']} ({r['ext_id']})",
                         _quote(r["comment"])), r["comment"],
                {k_: r[k_] for k_ in ("vehicle_line", "market_code", "polarity", "powertrain")}) for r in rows]


def filters() -> dict:
    """Values the UI can offer as filters: lines, markets, top-level domains, polarities, powertrains."""
    c = _conn()
    return {
        "lines": [r["key"] for r in c.execute(
            "select key from public.ontology where kind='vehicle_line' and active order by key")],
        "markets": [{"key": r["key"], "label": r["label"]} for r in c.execute(
            "select key, label from public.ontology where kind='market' and active order by key")],
        "domains": [{"key": r["key"], "label": r["label"]} for r in c.execute(
            "select key, label from public.ontology where kind='domain' and parent_id is null and active order by label")],
        "polarities": ["positive", "negative", "request"],
        "powertrains": ["ICE", "PHEV", "BEV"],
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- citations

def cite(kind: str, id: str) -> Citation:
    """Resolve any stored evidence row to its citation; raises if it does not exist."""
    r = _conn().execute("select kind, id, file, locator, text from public.evidence_item where kind = %s and id = %s",
                        (kind, id)).fetchone()
    if not r:
        raise LookupError(f"no {kind} evidence with id {id}")

Mention any `docs/decisions/` entry added or changed. 4. **Never push to `main` directly** unless the user explicitly says so; work on a branch and open a PR. Never force-push `main`. Force-pushing your own feature branch after a squash is fine (`--force-with-lease`). 5. **Never commit** `data/` (BMW-provided files), `.env`, or any secret. Check `git status` before committing; if any of those show up as staged, stop and fix `.gitignore`. ## Docs and design decisions - When a design decision changes, edit the relevant `docs/architecture/*.md` in place, bump its `Last updated` date, and add a dated entry in `docs/decisions/` (see `docs/decisions/README.md`). Do this in the same commit as the code change that motivated it. ## Syncing to Supabase after a push After a successful push, sync the project record to Supabase. Any agent can do this from a shell: 1. Run `python skills/database-setup/scripts/sync_docs.py` from a checkout of the pushed commit. It upserts `docs/decisions/*.md` into `design_decisions` and `docs/architecture/*.md` into `architecture_docs` with the commit sha. (Supabase MCP tools may be used instead if available.) 2. Schema changes go through `python skills/database-setup/scripts/apply_migration.py ` (try `--dry-run` first), never ad-hoc DDL, and the migration file is committed in the same squashed commit. 3. Check the current state with `python skills/database-setup/scripts/check_db.py` before changing schema, and review the Supabase advisors after DDL. 4. Report what was synced in the final message. If a sync step fails or is skipped, say so explicitly. Do not claim the sync is done. The git repo is the source of truth; Supabase is a mirror. Never edit docs only in Supabase. # Frontend style guide How the frontend is built and changed. Read with [`../design.md`](../design.md) (brand tokens), [`ui-design-guidelines.md`](ui-design-guidelines.md) (anti-slop workflow) and [decision 0021](decisions/0021-rounded-chat-first-frontend.md) (rounded, chat-first look). Where they disagree, 0021 wins on shape and elevation; `design.md` wins on colour and type. ## Stack Vite, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui (style `base-nova`, **Base UI** primitives, not Radix), lucide icons. Components live in `frontend/src/components/ui/`, features in `src/features//`, shared chrome in `src/components/layout/`. The UI talks only to `/api` through `src/lib/api.ts`. ## Look and feel | Aspect | Rule | |---|---| | Colour | White canvas, `canvas-tint` (#f6f7f9) behind white cards. BMW Blue (`primary`) is the only action colour. Semantic colours only for state. No gradients, glows, glass. | | Type | Inter Variable. Body 400, headings 600, no negative tracking beyond `-0.01em` on headings. | | Shape | `--radius` 0.75rem. Cards `rounded-2xl`, inputs and buttons `rounded-xl`, chat bubbles and composer `rounded-3xl`, chips and avatars pills. | | Elevation | `shadow-xs` on cards, `shadow-sm` on primary buttons, `shadow-md` on the composer and sign-in panel only. | | Icons | lucide only, `size-4` inline, `size-5` in headings. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden`. Never hand-draw SVG. | | Spacing | 4px scale. Page gutters `px-4 sm:px-8`. Chat column `max-w-3xl`, pages `max-w-6xl`. | | Motion | Only `.rise` (new messages) and `.typing-dot`. Both are disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`. | | Copy | Plain sentences, no em or en dashes, one verb per action ("Send", "Search", "Sign out"). No invented data: examples are labelled as examples. | ## Layout patterns - **Shell:** `App.tsx` holds a 288px sidebar (`components/layout/Sidebar.tsx`) and the main column. Below `md` the sidebar is a `Sheet`. - **Chat view:** `h-dvh` column, scrolling thread, composer pinned at the bottom. The empty state centres the composer. - **Content pages:** wrap in `PageShell` (icon, title, one-line description, scrolling body on `canvas-tint`). - **State shared across views** (chat list, open chat) lives in `features/research/chat-store.tsx`. Keep other state local. - Every async view has loading (layout-matched `Skeleton`), empty, error (`role="alert"`) and success states. ## Building a UI change: the workflow 1. **Read** `design.md`, `ui-design-guidelines.md` and this file. Skim the nearest existing feature for conventions. 2. **Pick components with the shadcn MCP** before writing markup: - `search_items_in_registries` / `list_items_in_registries` to find a component or block, - `view_items_in_registries` and `get_item_examples_from_registries` to read source and usage, - `get_add_command_for_items` for the install command, then run `npx shadcn@latest add @shadcn/`. - If the MCP is not connected, the CLI does the same (`npx shadcn@latest search`, `view`, `add`). Do not recreate a shadcn component by hand. 3. **Use the design skills.** Invoke the `frontend-design` skill for hierarchy and typography choices and the `vercel:shadcn` skill for composition and theming. State the reading ("Reading this as: for ...") from the guidelines. 4. **Check what the CLI generated** (see pitfalls). Adjust the new file to the tokens above instead of overriding it at every call site. 5. **Iterate visually with Playwright.** Start the dev server, mock `/api` with `page.route` (reuse `tests/helpers.ts`: `withSession`, `json`), screenshot desktop (1440x1000) and mobile (iPhone 13) to the scratchpad, look at the images, fix, repeat. Do at least: empty state, populated state, working/loading, error, and the mobile menu. Delete throwaway screenshot specs afterwards. 6. **Verify:** `npm run build` (type-check), `npx oxlint`, `npx playwright test` (desktop and mobile, includes an axe WCAG AA check on each page). 7. **Docs:** a changed design rule needs an edit here or in `design.md` plus a dated entry in `docs/decisions/`, in the same commit. ## Accessibility (enforced by the axe checks) - Visible `

"""Read-only evidence endpoints. Everything returned carries a citation resolved from the stored row."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import asdict
from typing import Annotated
from uuid import UUID

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Query

from app.knowledge import library, tools

from .schemas import (CitationOut, EvidenceContextOut, EvidenceKind, GroupBy, HitOut, Line, Market, Polarity, Powertrain,
                      SearchResponse, StatRow, StatsResponse)

router = APIRouter(prefix="/evidence", tags=["evidence"])


def _unavailable(e: Exception) -> HTTPException:
    """Turn infrastructure errors into a 503 without leaking connection details."""
    return HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=f"evidence store unavailable ({type(e).__name__})")


def _hit(h: tools.Hit) -> HitOut:
    return HitOut(citation=CitationOut(**asdict(h.citation)), text=h.text, meta=h.meta, score=h.score)


@router.get("/search", response_model=SearchResponse)
def search(
    q: Annotated[str, Query(min_length=2, max_length=300)],
    source: Annotated[str, Query(pattern="^(feedback|docs)$")] = "feedback",
    line: Line | None = None,
    market: Market | None = None,
    domain: Annotated[str | None, Query(max_length=60)] = None,
    polarity: Polarity | None = None,
    powertrain: Powertrain | None = None,
    k: Annotated[int, Query(ge=1, le=50)] = 10,
) -> SearchResponse:
    try:
        if source == "docs":
            hits = tools.search_docs(q, line=line, k=k)
        else:
            hits = tools.search_feedback(q, line=line, market=market, domain=domain, polarity=polarity,
                                         powertrain=powertrain, k=k)
    except ValueError as e:  # unknown domain
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=str(e))
    except Exception as e:
        raise _unavailable(e)
    return SearchResponse(query=q, source=source, hits=[_hit(h) for h in hits])


@router.get("/stats", response_model=StatsResponse)
def stats(
    group_by: GroupBy,
    line: Line | None = None,
    market: Market | None = None,
    domain: Annotated[str | None, Query(max_length=60)] = None,
    polarity: Polarity | None = None,
    powertrain: Powertrain | None = None,
) -> StatsResponse:
    try:
        rows = tools.feedback_stats(group_by, line=line, market=market, domain=domain, polarity=polarity,
                                    powertrain=powertrain)
    except ValueError as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=str(e))
    except Exception as e:
        raise _unavailable(e)
    return StatsResponse(group_by=group_by, total=sum(r["n"] for r in rows),
                         rows=[StatRow(key=r["key"], n=r["n"]) for r in rows])


@router.get("/filters")
def filters() -> dict:
    try:
        return tools.filters()
    except Exception as e:
        raise _unavailable(e)


@router.get("/{kind}/{evidence_id}/context", response_model=EvidenceContextOut)
def context(kind: EvidenceKind, evidence_id: UUID) -> dict:
    """The cited passage in its surroundings (the whole catalog page, the neighbouring comments) for the viewer."""
    try:
        return library.evidence_context(kind, str(evidence_id))
    except LookupError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="no such evidence row")
    except Exception as e:
        raise _unavailable(e)


@router.get("/{kind}/{evidence_id}", response_model=CitationOut)
def cite(kind: EvidenceKind, evidence_id: UUID) -> CitationOut:
    try:
        c = tools.cite(kind, str(evidence_id))
    except LookupError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="no such evidence row")
    except Exception as e:
        raise _unavailable(e)
    return CitationOut(**asdict(c))

# Scaling & configuration

> Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (chat wording)

Nothing about G60 or "Europe" is hardcoded. Every `PipelineRun` (one per chat request) takes a config:
`{vehicle_line, market, generation_baseline}`, read from the PM's message or asked back by the
orchestrator if missing. Swapping to the 1 Series in China is a config
change, not a rewrite.

## Domain taxonomy is config, not code

Exterior / Interior / Powertrain / Driver Assistance / Infotainment / Comfort & Space / Usability
/ Variant & Package / Range & Charging / Safety (flagged out of scope) — stored as an editable `Ontology` store (see
[`04-data-model.md`](04-data-model.md#ontology)), not a hardcoded enum, so a future BEV-only line
can extend it without a code change.

## New source = one adapter

Every ingestion agent implements the same `Source → Finding[]` interface (see
[`03-ingestion.md`](03-ingestion.md)). A new feedback export, a new web source, a new internal
system plugs in without touching clustering, drafting, or scoring.

## Markets compose, they don't collapse

A requirement can carry per-market sub-scores and a market-fit flag ("fits EU, doesn't fit China")
rather than forcing one global priority — this is the direct answer to the PM pain point raised
about balancing requirements across regions with different climate, usage, and culture.

## Regulatory guardrail

Findings that read as safety/emissions/type-approval or pricing/business-case in nature are
auto-tagged by the Clustering/Ontology Agent and routed to a visibly separate "flagged, out of
scope" bin — never drafted into a customer requirement. Keeps the demo honestly inside the brief's
boundary instead of silently drifting into engineering or regulatory territory.
# 0021 — Chat-first frontend with rounded components and soft elevation

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted · Amends the shape and elevation rules of [`design.md`](../../design.md) and [`ui-design-guidelines.md`](../ui-design-guidelines.md); builds on [0017](0017-minimal-live-only-frontend.md)

## Context

The frontend looked like a plain document site: a top bar, a text-only conversation list beside the thread, and
rectangular, hairline-bordered components. The product is a research conversation, so it should read like a modern
chat app. The user asked explicitly for rounded edges, icons, and chat history on the left.

## Decision

1. **Layout.** A left sidebar (fixed on desktop, a sheet below `md`) holds the brand, New chat, the three views, the
   chat history grouped by recency, the account menu and the backend status. The Research view is a centred thread with
   a rounded composer, an empty state with example questions, and a typing indicator while an agent works.
2. **Shape.** `--radius` is 0.75rem. Cards, inputs, buttons and menus are rounded; chips and avatars are pills.
   This overrides the "rectangular components" default in `design.md`.
3. **Elevation.** Three soft shadow tokens (`xs`, `sm`, `md`) replace "no drop shadows"; they are used only on the composer,
   cards and the sign-in panel. Depth otherwise still comes from surface contrast (`canvas-tint` behind white cards).
4. **Unchanged brand rules.** BMW Blue stays the only action colour, white canvas, Inter as the substitute typeface, light
   theme only, no gradients or glows. Body weight is now 400 and headings 600 (was 300 and 700) for legibility in dense chat text.
5. **One icon family** (lucide, already in the project) and shadcn components on Base UI (`avatar`, `dropdown-menu`,
   `scroll-area`, `sheet`, `tooltip`).

## Consequences

Brand fidelity to BMW's corporate site is looser on purpose; the product is an internal tool, not a marketing page.
Tests that reach the sidebar open the sheet first on small screens (`openMenu` and `closeMenu` in `tests/helpers.ts`).

export class ApiError extends Error {
  status: number
  constructor(status: number, message: string) {
    super(message)
    this.status = status
  }
}

function query(params: Record<string, string | number | undefined>): string {
  const q = new URLSearchParams()
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(params)) if (v !== undefined && v !== '') q.set(k, String(v))
  return q.toString()
}

async function request<T>(method: string, path: string, body?: unknown, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<T> {
  let res: Response
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {}
  if (body !== undefined) headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
  const token = getToken()
  if (token) headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`
  try {
    res = await fetch(`/api${path}`, {
      method,
      signal,
      headers,
      body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
    })
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof DOMException && e.name === 'AbortError') throw e
    throw new ApiError(0, 'Cannot reach the backend. Is it running?')
  }
  // 401 from anywhere but the login call itself means the session is gone: the UI then asks for a sign-in.
  if (res.status === 401 && path !== '/auth/login') {
    markRequired()
    throw new ApiError(401, 'Sign in to continue.')
  }
  if (res.status === 204) return undefined as T
  if (!res.ok) {
    let detail = res.statusText
    try {
      const body = await res.json()
      if (typeof body.detail === 'string') detail = body.detail
      else if (Array.isArray(body.detail)) detail = body.detail.map((d: { msg: string }) => d.msg).join('; ')
    } catch {
      /* keep statusText */
    }
    throw new ApiError(res.status, detail)
  }
  return res.json() as Promise<T>
}

const get = <T>(path: string, signal?: AbortSignal) => request<T>('GET', path, undefined, signal)

export const api = {
  health: (signal?: AbortSignal) => get<Health>('/health', signal),
  filters: (signal?: AbortSignal) => get<FilterOptions>('/evidence/filters', signal),
  search: (q: string, source: SearchSource, f: EvidenceFilters, signal?: AbortSignal) =>
    get<SearchResponse>(`/evidence/search?${query({ q, source, ...f })}`, signal),
  stats: (groupBy: GroupBy, f: EvidenceFilters, signal?: AbortSignal) =>
    get<StatsResponse>(`/evidence/stats?${query({ group_by: groupBy, ...f })}`, signal),
  login: (email: string, password: string) => request<LoginResult>('POST', '/auth/login', { email, password }),
  me: (signal?: AbortSignal) => get<AuthUser>('/auth/me', signal),
  logout: () => request<void>('POST', '/auth/logout'),
  evidenceContext: (kind: string, id: string, signal?: AbortSignal) =>
    get<EvidenceContext>(`/evidence/${kind}/${id}/context`, signal),
  sources: (signal?: AbortSignal) => get<SourceInfo[]>('/sources', signal),
  coverage: (signal?: AbortSignal) => get<Coverage>('/evidence/coverage', signal),
  conversations: (signal?: AbortSignal) => get<Conversation[]>('/conversations', signal),

export async function fetchSourceFile(sourceId: string): Promise<Blob> {

def _unavailable(e: Exception) -> HTTPException:
    """Turn infrastructure errors into a 503 without leaking connection details."""
    return HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=f"evidence store unavailable ({type(e).__name__})")


def _hit(h: tools.Hit) -> HitOut:
    return HitOut(citation=CitationOut(**asdict(h.citation)), text=h.text, meta=h.meta, score=h.score)


@router.get("/search", response_model=SearchResponse)
def search(
    q: Annotated[str, Query(min_length=2, max_length=300)],
    source: Annotated[str, Query(pattern="^(feedback|docs)$")] = "feedback",
    line: Line | None = None,
    market: Market | None = None,
    domain: Annotated[str | None, Query(max_length=60)] = None,
    polarity: Polarity | None = None,
    powertrain: Powertrain | None = None,
    k: Annotated[int, Query(ge=1, le=50)] = 10,
) -> SearchResponse:
    try:
        if source == "docs":
            hits = tools.search_docs(q, line=line, k=k)
        else:
            hits = tools.search_feedback(q, line=line, market=market, domain=domain, polarity=polarity,
                                         powertrain=powertrain, k=k)
    except ValueError as e:  # unknown domain
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=str(e))
    except Exception as e:
        raise _unavailable(e)
    return SearchResponse(query=q, source=source, hits=[_hit(h) for h in hits])


@router.get("/stats", response_model=StatsResponse)
def stats(
    group_by: GroupBy,
    line: Line | None = None,
    market: Market | None = None,
    domain: Annotated[str | None, Query(max_length=60)] = None,
    polarity: Polarity | None = None,
    powertrain: Powertrain | None = None,
) -> StatsResponse:
    try:
        rows = tools.feedback_stats(group_by, line=line, market=market, domain=domain, polarity=polarity,
                                    powertrain=powertrain)
    except ValueError as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=str(e))
    except Exception as e:
        raise _unavailable(e)
    return StatsResponse(group_by=group_by, total=sum(r["n"] for r in rows),

def filters() -> dict:

def context(kind: EvidenceKind, evidence_id: UUID) -> dict:

    try:

interface Props {
  id: string
  label: string
  value: string | undefined
  options: { value: string; label: string }[]
  onChange: (value: string | undefined) => void
  allLabel?: string
}

const ALL = '__all__'

// Label above the control, as the design guidelines require; "All" clears the filter.
export function FilterSelect({ id, label, value, options, onChange, allLabel = 'All' }: Props) {
  const items = [{ value: ALL, label: allLabel }, ...options]
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
      <Label htmlFor={id}>{label}</Label>
      <Select items={items} value={value ?? ALL} onValueChange={(v) => onChange(!v || v === ALL ? undefined : v)}>
        <SelectTrigger id={id} className="w-full">
          <SelectValue />
        </SelectTrigger>
        <SelectContent>
          {items.map((o) => (
            <SelectItem key={o.value} value={o.value}>
              {o.label}
            </SelectItem>
          ))}
        </SelectContent>
      </Select>
    </div>
  )
}

> Status: `draft` · Last updated: 2026-10-10 (chat wording)

Nothing about G60 or "Europe" is hardcoded. Every `PipelineRun` (one per chat request) takes a config:
`{vehicle_line, market, generation_baseline}`, read from the PM's message or asked back by the
orchestrator if missing. Swapping to the 1 Series in China is a config
change, not a rewrite.

## Domain taxonomy is config, not code

Exterior / Interior / Powertrain / Driver Assistance / Infotainment / Comfort & Space / Usability
/ Variant & Package / Range & Charging / Safety (flagged out of scope) — stored as an editable `Ontology` store (see
[`04-data-model.md`](04-data-model.md#ontology)), not a hardcoded enum, so a future BEV-only line
can extend it without a code change.

## New source = one adapter

Every ingestion agent implements the same `Source → Finding[]` interface (see
[`03-ingestion.md`](03-ingestion.md)). A new feedback export, a new web source, a new internal
system plugs in without touching clustering, drafting, or scoring.

## Markets compose, they don't collapse

A requirement can carry per-market sub-scores and a market-fit flag ("fits EU, doesn't fit China")
rather than forcing one global priority — this is the direct answer to the PM pain point raised
about balancing requirements across regions with different climate, usage, and culture.

## Regulatory guardrail

Findings that read as safety/emissions/type-approval or pricing/business-case in nature are
auto-tagged by the Clustering/Ontology Agent and routed to a visibly separate "flagged, out of
scope" bin — never drafted into a customer requirement. Keeps the demo honestly inside the brief's
boundary instead of silently drifting into engineering or regulatory territory.
# 0021 — Chat-first frontend with rounded components and soft elevation

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted · Amends the shape and elevation rules of [`design.md`](../../design.md) and [`ui-design-guidelines.md`](../ui-design-guidelines.md); builds on [0017](0017-minimal-live-only-frontend.md)

## Context

The frontend looked like a plain document site: a top bar, a text-only conversation list beside the thread, and
rectangular, hairline-bordered components. The product is a research conversation, so it should read like a modern
chat app. The user asked explicitly for rounded edges, icons, and chat history on the left.

## Decision

1. **Layout.** A left sidebar (fixed on desktop, a sheet below `md`) holds the brand, New chat, the three views, the
   chat history grouped by recency, the account menu and the backend status. The Research view is a centred thread with
   a rounded composer, an empty state with example questions, and a typing indicator while an agent works.
2. **Shape.** `--radius` is 0.75rem. Cards, inputs, buttons and menus are rounded; chips and avatars are pills.
   This overrides the "rectangular components" default in `design.md`.
3. **Elevation.** Three soft shadow tokens (`xs`, `sm`, `md`) replace "no drop shadows"; they are used only on the composer,
   cards and the sign-in panel. Depth otherwise still comes from surface contrast (`canvas-tint` behind white cards).
4. **Unchanged brand rules.** BMW Blue stays the only action colour, white canvas, Inter as the substitute typeface, light
   theme only, no gradients or glows. Body weight is now 400 and headings 600 (was 300 and 700) for legibility in dense chat text.
5. **One icon family** (lucide, already in the project) and shadcn components on Base UI (`avatar`, `dropdown-menu`,
   `scroll-area`, `sheet`, `tooltip`).

## Consequences

Brand fidelity to BMW's corporate site is looser on purpose; the product is an internal tool, not a marketing page.
Tests that reach the sidebar open the sheet first on small screens (`openMenu` and `closeMenu` in `tests/helpers.ts`).
