L0: ---
L1: name: frontend-design
L2: description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
L3: license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
L4: ---
L5: # Frontend Design
L6: 
L7: Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.
L8: ## Ground your designs in the subject matter
L9: If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint.
L10: The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.
L11: ## Design principles
L12: 
L13: For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.
L14: Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.
L15: Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.
L16: Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.
L17: 
L18: Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
L19: - Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
L20: - Using all caps for labels.
L21: - Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.
L22: Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.
L23: Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.
L24: Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.
L25: ## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique
L26: For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
L27: 1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
L28: 2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
L29: 3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
L30: 4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
L31: 5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.
L32: All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.
L33: As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.
L34: Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
L35: - Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
L36: - Type: the typefaces and their roles.
L37: - Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
L38: - Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.
L39: Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.
L40: When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.
L41: ## Restraint and self-critique
L42: Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens.
L43: Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.
L44: ## More on writing in design
L45: 
L46: Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.
L47: Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.
L48: Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.
L49: Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.
L50: 
L51: Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

L141: cite83†Previous cite84†Next L142: 
L143: Give your AI assistant deep knowledge of shadcn/ui components, patterns, and best practices.
L144: 
L145: Skills give AI assistants like Claude Code project-aware context about shadcn/ui. When installed, your AI assistant knows how to find, install, compose, and customize components using the correct APIs and patterns for your project.
L146: 
L147: For example, you can ask your AI assistant to:
L148:   * "Add a login form with email and password fields."
L149:   * "Create a settings page with a form for updating profile information."
L150:   * "Build a dashboard with a sidebar, stats cards, and a data table."
L151:   * "Switch to --preset [CODE]"
L152:   * "Can you add a hero from @tailark?"
L153: 
L154: The skill reads your project's `components.json` and provides the assistant with your framework, aliases, installed components, icon library, and base library so it can generate correct code on the first try.
L155: 
L156: * * *
L157: ## cite110†Install# L158: 
L159:     [Button: pnpm][Button: npm][Button: yarn][Button: bun]
L160: 
L161:     `pnpm dlx skills add shadcn/ui`
L162: 
L163: Copy
L164: 
L165: This installs the shadcn skill into your project. Once installed, your AI assistant automatically loads it when working with shadcn/ui components.
L166: 
L167: Learn more about skills at cite111†skills.sh†skills.sh .
L168: 
L169: * * *
L170: 
L171: ## cite112†What's Included# L172: 
L173: The skill provides your AI assistant with the following knowledge:
L174: ### cite113†Project Context# L175: 
L176: On every interaction, the skill runs `shadcn info --json` to get your project's configuration: framework, Tailwind version, aliases, base library (`base`, `radix`, or `aria`), icon library, installed components, and resolved file paths.
L177: 
L178: ### cite114†CLI Commands# L179: 
L180: Full reference for all CLI commands: `init`, `add`, `search`, `view`, `docs`, `diff`, `info`, and `build`. Includes flags, dry-run mode, smart merge workflows, presets, and templates.
L181: ### cite115†Theming and Customization# L182: 
L183: How CSS variables, OKLCH colors, dark mode, custom colors, border radius, and component variants work. Includes guidance for both Tailwind v3 and v4.
L184: 
L185: ### cite116†Registry Authoring# L186: 
L187: How to build and publish custom component registries: `registry.json` format, item types, file objects, dependencies, CSS variables, building, hosting, and user configuration.
L188: ### cite117†MCP Server# L189: 
L190: Setup and tools for the shadcn MCP server, which lets AI assistants search, browse, and install components from registries.
L191: 
L192: * * *
L193: ## cite118†How It Works# L194:   1. Project detection — The skill activates when it finds a `components.json` file in your project.
L195:   2. Context injection — It runs `shadcn info --json` to read your project configuration and injects the result into the assistant's context.
L196:   3. Pattern enforcement — The assistant follows shadcn/ui composition rules: using `FieldGroup` for forms, `ToggleGroup` for option sets, semantic colors, and correct base-specific APIs.
L197:   4. Component discovery — The assistant uses `shadcn docs`, `shadcn search`, or MCP tools to find components and their documentation before generating code.
L198: ## cite119†Learn More# L199: 
L200:   * cite11†CLI — Full CLI command reference
L201:   * cite120†MCP Server — Connect the MCP server for registry access

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.api import evidence, health
from app.knowledge.tools import Citation, Hit
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)


def fake_hit(kind="feedback"):
    return Hit(Citation(kind, "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111", "G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx",
                        "sheet Feedback_Explorer, row 4642 (G60-3695)", "They barely cool anything"),
               "They barely cool anything", {"vehicle_line": "G60", "similarity": 0.71}, 0.03)


def test_health_reports_degraded_without_services(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(health, "check_db", lambda: "not_configured")
    r = client.get("/api/health")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert body["db"] == "not_configured"
    assert body["status"] == "degraded"
    assert "postgres" not in r.text.lower() and "password" not in r.text.lower()


def test_search_returns_hits_with_citations(monkeypatch):
    seen = {}

    def fake(q, **kw):
        seen.update(q=q, **kw)
        return [fake_hit()]

    monkeypatch.setattr(evidence.tools, "search_feedback", fake)
    r = client.get("/api/evidence/search", params={"q": "seat ventilation", "line": "G60", "polarity": "negative"})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    hit = r.json()["hits"][0]
    assert hit["citation"]["file"] == "G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx"
    assert hit["citation"]["locator"].startswith("sheet Feedback_Explorer, row 4642")
    assert hit["citation"]["quote"]
    assert seen["line"] == "G60" and seen["polarity"] == "negative" and seen["k"] == 10


def test_docs_source_uses_docs_search(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(evidence.tools, "search_docs", lambda q, **kw: [fake_hit("pdf_text")])
    r = client.get("/api/evidence/search", params={"q": "Felgen", "source": "docs"})
    assert r.json()["source"] == "docs" and r.json()["hits"][0]["citation"]["kind"] == "pdf_text"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("params", [
    {"q": "x"},                                      # too short
    {"q": "seats", "line": "X99"},                   # unknown line
    {"q": "seats", "market": "MARS"},                # unknown market
    {"q": "seats", "k": 500},                        # too many
    {"q": "seats", "source": "tables"},              # unknown source
])
def test_bad_parameters_are_rejected_before_any_lookup(params, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(evidence.tools, "search_feedback", lambda *a, **k: pytest.fail("must not be called"))
    assert client.get("/api/evidence/search", params=params).status_code == 422


def test_unknown_domain_is_a_422(monkeypatch):
    def boom(*a, **k):
        raise ValueError("unknown domain: nope")
    monkeypatch.setattr(evidence.tools, "search_feedback", boom)
    r = client.get("/api/evidence/search", params={"q": "seats", "domain": "nope"})
    assert r.status_code == 422 and "unknown domain" in r.json()["detail"]


def test_store_outage_is_a_503_without_details(monkeypatch):
    def boom(*a, **k):
        raise RuntimeError("password=secret host=db.example")
    monkeypatch.setattr(evidence.tools, "search_feedback", boom)
    r = client.get("/api/evidence/search", params={"q": "seats"})
    assert r.status_code == 503
    assert "secret" not in r.text and "db.example" not in r.text


def test_stats_sums_the_total(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(evidence.tools, "feedback_stats",
                        lambda group_by, **kw: [{"key": "US", "n": 1594}, {"key": "EU", "n": 72}])
    body = client.get("/api/evidence/stats", params={"group_by": "market_code", "line": "G60"}).json()
    assert body["total"] == 1666 and body["rows"][0] == {"key": "US", "n": 1594}


def test_cite_unknown_row_is_404_and_bad_id_is_422(monkeypatch):
    def missing(kind, id):
        raise LookupError("nope")
    monkeypatch.setattr(evidence.tools, "cite", missing)

    assert client.get("/api/evidence/spreadsheet/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000").status_code == 422

# Agent rules

Project: BMW hackathon requirement-evidence engine. Architecture docs live in `docs/`
(start at `docs/README.md`); those `.md` files are the source of truth.

## Repository layout

- `backend/` FastAPI app and Python package `app` (`api/`, `knowledge/`, `agents/`, `ingest/`,
  `orchestration/`), tests in `backend/tests/`. Run with `make backend`, test with `make test`.
- `frontend/` Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui. Run with `make frontend`, build with `make build`.
- `supabase/migrations/` SQL migrations, `docs/` architecture and decisions, `skills/` agent skills,
  `data/` provided BMW files (gitignored). One `.env` at the repo root. See `docs/architecture/12-repo-structure.md`.
- The frontend talks to the backend only through `/api`; it never touches the database directly.
- Put new Python code under `backend/app/`, import it as `app.<package>`, and run scripts as
  `python -m app.<package>.<module>`.

## UI design

- Before generating or changing UI, read `design.md`, `docs/ui-design-guidelines.md` and `docs/frontend-style-guide.md`.
  Find and add components with the shadcn MCP (or `npx shadcn@latest`), use the `frontend-design` skill, and review the
  result in screenshots with Playwright at desktop and mobile sizes before delivering.
- Use the BMW tokens and component rules in `design.md` for all UI.
- Apply the anti-slop workflow in `docs/ui-design-guidelines.md`. BMW's explicit brand rules
  take precedence over generic aesthetic defaults, including white surfaces and the Inter fallback.
  Shape and elevation follow decision 0021 (rounded components, soft shadows), not the rectangular default.

## Database

- Postgres on Supabase (pgvector). To connect, set up a machine or teammate, check the state, apply
  migrations, load data or fix a connection error, read `skills/database-setup/SKILL.md` first.
- Check the connection with `python skills/database-setup/scripts/check_db.py --openai`.
- Never print, log, commit or paste secrets (`SUPABASE_DB_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, passwords, keys).
- **Every API route needs a signed-in user by default.** New routers go into the `protected` router in
  `backend/app/api/__init__.py`. Only `/api/health` and `/api/auth/login` are public; a test checks every route, so do
  not add to the public list without a decision record. Never print or commit tokens or passwords; users are created
  by a human with `python -m app.auth.manage`.
- Agents read evidence through `backend/app/knowledge/tools.py`, not hand-written SQL.

## Pushing

1. **Only push when the user asks.** Never push on your own initiative.
2. **Always squash before pushing.** Collapse all local work since the branch diverged from
   `main` into a single commit (`git reset --soft $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)` then
   commit, or `git merge-base` + `git rebase -i` equivalent without interactive flags). One push
   = one commit.
3. **Commit message:** imperative subject line, then a short body listing what changed and why.
   Mention any `docs/decisions/` entry added or changed.
4. **Never push to `main` directly** unless the user explicitly says so; work on a branch and
   open a PR. Never force-push `main`. Force-pushing your own feature branch after a squash is
   fine (`--force-with-lease`).
5. **Never commit** `data/` (BMW-provided files), `.env`, or any secret. Check `git status`
   before committing; if any of those show up as staged, stop and fix `.gitignore`.

## Docs and design decisions

- When a design decision changes, edit the relevant `docs/architecture/*.md` in place, bump its
  `Last updated` date, and add a dated entry in `docs/decisions/` (see `docs/decisions/README.md`).
  Do this in the same commit as the code change that motivated it.

## Syncing to Supabase after a push

After a successful push, sync the project record to Supabase. Any agent can do this from a shell:

1. Run `python skills/database-setup/scripts/sync_docs.py` from a checkout of the pushed commit. It
   upserts `docs/decisions/*.md` into `design_decisions` and `docs/architecture/*.md` into
   `architecture_docs` with the commit sha. (Supabase MCP tools may be used instead if available.)
2. Schema changes go through `python skills/database-setup/scripts/apply_migration.py <file>`
   (try `--dry-run` first), never ad-hoc DDL, and the migration file is committed in the same
   squashed commit.
3. Check the current state with `python skills/database-setup/scripts/check_db.py` before changing
   schema, and review the Supabase advisors after DDL.
4. Report what was synced in the final message. If a sync step fails or is skipped, say so
   explicitly. Do not claim the sync is done.

The git repo is the source of truth; Supabase is a mirror. Never edit docs only in Supabase.
# UI design guidelines

Project-specific adaptation of the supplied `design-taste-frontend` guidance.
Read alongside [`../design.md`](../design.md), which defines the BMW design system.

## Scope and precedence

Use BMW tokens for every generated UI. Apply the marketing-page guidance below to landing
pages, portfolios, editorial pages, and redesigns. Do not impose marketing hero, photography,
section variety, or short-copy requirements on the requirement-evidence engine's dashboards,
data tables, agent review screens, or multi-step product workflows. Those screens need clear
information hierarchy, evidence, accessible controls, and complete interaction states.

Explicit user instructions and BMW brand rules override generic taste defaults. In particular:

- Pure white canvas, BMW Blue `#1c69d4`, dark navy hero bands, and 700/300 typography remain.
- Inter is an approved substitute when licensed BMW Type Next Latin is unavailable.
- Components are rounded (`--radius` 0.75rem) with soft `xs`/`sm`/`md` shadows, per [decision 0021](decisions/0021-rounded-chat-first-frontend.md).
  This replaces the earlier rectangular, no-shadow default.
- Light surfaces with dark hero or CTA bands are intentional BMW composition.
- Do not invent a dark theme unless requested; the supplied brand system defines a light base.
- M stripes belong only in M-model or motorsport contexts.

## Before implementation

1. Infer page kind, audience, existing brand, assets, and accessibility constraints.
2. State: "Reading this as: <page kind> for <audience>, with a <vibe> language,
   leaning toward <design system or aesthetic family>."
3. Set `DESIGN_VARIANCE`, `MOTION_INTENSITY`, and `VISUAL_DENSITY` explicitly.
   For measured BMW corporate marketing, start at 4 / 3 / 4; adapt to the brief.
4. For redesigns, audit tokens, information architecture, content, interactions, accessibility,
   analytics, and SEO before editing. Preserve routes, nav labels, form names/order, brand marks,
   and legal/consent copy unless the user authorizes changes.
5. For a specific visual reference, record concrete ratios, spacing, colors, radii, shadows,
   icon treatment, layout structure, and deliberate omissions. Mark estimates as estimates.
   Write a yes/no check for each rule and verify the composition can be rebuilt from the rules.
6. Inspect the existing stack and `package.json` before importing dependencies. Reuse the
   project's foundation; do not mix component systems or recreate an explicitly requested
   official design system by hand.

## Composition and copy

- Use the BMW spacing scale, 80px major section rhythm, 24px card padding, and 1440px container.
- Prefer purposeful alignment and real content hierarchy over decorative asymmetry.
- Marketing heroes: at most two desktop headline lines, 20 words of supporting copy,
  one primary and at most one secondary CTA. Keep CTAs visible in the initial viewport.
  Limit desktop top padding to 96px and hero text to four elements total.
- Keep desktop navigation on one line and 64px tall, with an 80px maximum.
- Use at most one section eyebrow per three marketing sections. Avoid numbered sections,
  scroll cues, version stamps, decorative status dots, atmospheric locale strips, and
  decoration text at the hero's bottom.
- Avoid repeated generic feature-card rows, empty bento cells, and three consecutive
  alternating image/text splits. Choose layouts that fit the actual content.
- Put supporting paragraphs directly below headings; avoid floating corner explainers.
- Keep marketing paragraphs short and quotes within three lines. Use disclosures, grouped
  content, or separate pages for long lists rather than dumping data into landing pages.
- Use plain, grammatical copy. Avoid forced metaphors, filler verbs, invented testimonials,
  fabricated metrics, and fake precision. Label sample data explicitly.
- Use one label per CTA intent and one verb per action throughout the product.
- Generated visible UI copy uses regular hyphens, commas, periods, or parentheses instead
  of em-dashes or en-dash separators. Preserve supplied source material as supplied.

## Assets and styling

- Use real brand assets and real component previews. Never fabricate screenshot-like
  rectangles, terminal windows, or dashboards as decorative product previews.
- For marketing surfaces needing photography, prefer suitable generated assets when tools
  are available, then verified real imagery. If assets cannot be obtained, use clearly marked
  placeholders and report the missing placements. Product workflows do not need stock imagery.
- Use real logos for genuine social proof; do not invent customers or decorative photo credits.
- Keep images free of decorative pills and labels. Reserve dimensions to prevent layout shifts.
- Use one icon family. Prefer Phosphor, HugeIcons, Radix, or Tabler; retain Lucide if already
  used by the project. Do not hand-draw SVG icon paths.
- Avoid gradient text, glows, glass panels, random accent colors, custom cursors, and ornamental
  grid lines. BMW photography and surface contrast provide depth.
- Self-host fonts with `font-display: swap`, or use `next/font` in Next.js.

## Interaction and engineering

- Provide meaningful loading, empty, error, disabled, selected, focus, and success states
  where the interaction requires them. Use layout-matched skeletons for loading.
- Put labels above form inputs, helper text alongside the field, and inline errors below.
  Placeholders are never labels. Ensure keyboard operation and visible focus.
- Check text, placeholders, focus indicators, and controls for WCAG AA contrast. Keep CTA
  labels on one desktop line and touch targets at least 48px where BMW specifies them.
- Use CSS Grid for grids and declare each multi-column layout's mobile collapse explicitly.
  Use `min-height: 100dvh` when a full-height layout is needed, rather than fixed `100vh`.
- Keep state local unless shared state is necessary. Put providers and interactive islands
  in Client Components in Next.js; static layouts can remain Server Components.
- Animate only when motion explains hierarchy, feedback, storytelling, or state changes.
  Honor reduced motion. Do not claim motion that has not been implemented.
- Use Motion values for continuous pointer/scroll values, never React state. Avoid raw scroll
  listeners. Use IntersectionObserver, CSS scroll animations, Motion, or GSAP ScrollTrigger.
- Isolate animation code in client leaves and clean up effects. Do not let animation libraries
  compete over the same elements. Keep marquees to at most one per marketing page.
- For actual GSAP pinned stacks or horizontal pans, pin at `start: "top top"` and use correct
  end distances and scrub behavior. Do not add scroll hijacks merely for decoration.
- Keep z-index layers intentional, lazy-load heavy below-the-fold code, and avoid grain filters
  on scrolling containers. Target LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, and CLS < 0.1.

## Pre-flight before delivery

Check applicable rules; mark out-of-scope items as such rather than inventing content to satisfy
them. Fix failures before delivering and report any checks that could not be run.

- Brief, mode, dials, reference rules, and BMW precedence are explicit.
- Colors, fonts, radii, spacing, and component states match `design.md`.
- Visible copy is grammatical, consistent, and free of decorative dash separators or fake data.
- Navigation, hero, CTAs, grids, and images fit desktop and mobile without overflow or clipping.
- Section layouts and eyebrow counts fit the marketing composition, with no empty filler cells.
- Assets load, previews are real, and social proof has a factual basis.
- Buttons, inputs, text, focus states, keyboard paths, and touch targets pass accessibility checks.
- Loading, empty, error, and disabled states work for relevant interactions.
- Motion is motivated, implemented, cleaned up, and disabled or simplified under reduced motion.
- Test every supported theme; do not require an invented theme merely to satisfy a generic rule.
- Run appropriate build checks and inspect the UI at desktop and mobile sizes. For marketing
  pages, run Lighthouse when a runnable browser environment is available; report measured
  results honestly instead of asserting Core Web Vitals from code inspection alone.
# Frontend style guide

How the frontend is built and changed. Read with [`../design.md`](../design.md) (brand tokens),
[`ui-design-guidelines.md`](ui-design-guidelines.md) (anti-slop workflow) and
[decision 0021](decisions/0021-rounded-chat-first-frontend.md) (rounded, chat-first look).
Where they disagree, 0021 wins on shape and elevation; `design.md` wins on colour and type.

## Stack

Vite, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui (style `base-nova`, **Base UI** primitives, not Radix), lucide icons.
Components live in `frontend/src/components/ui/`, features in `src/features/<name>/`, shared chrome in
`src/components/layout/`. The UI talks only to `/api` through `src/lib/api.ts`.

## Look and feel

| Aspect | Rule |
|---|---|
| Colour | White canvas, `canvas-tint` (#f6f7f9) behind white cards. BMW Blue (`primary`) is the only action colour. Semantic colours only for state. No gradients, glows, glass. |
| Type | Inter Variable. Body 400, headings 600, no negative tracking beyond `-0.01em` on headings. |
| Shape | `--radius` 0.75rem. Cards `rounded-2xl`, inputs and buttons `rounded-xl`, chat bubbles and composer `rounded-3xl`, chips and avatars pills. |
| Elevation | `shadow-xs` on cards, `shadow-sm` on primary buttons, `shadow-md` on the composer and sign-in panel only. |
| Icons | lucide only, `size-4` inline, `size-5` in headings. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden`. Never hand-draw SVG. |
| Spacing | 4px scale. Page gutters `px-4 sm:px-8`. Chat column `max-w-3xl`, pages `max-w-6xl`. |
| Motion | Only `.rise` (new messages) and `.typing-dot`. Both are disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`. |
| Copy | Plain sentences, no em or en dashes, one verb per action ("Send", "Search", "Sign out"). No invented data: examples are labelled as examples. |

## Layout patterns

- **Shell:** `App.tsx` holds a 288px sidebar (`components/layout/Sidebar.tsx`) and the main column. Below `md` the sidebar is a `Sheet`.
- **Chat view:** `h-dvh` column, scrolling thread, composer pinned at the bottom. The empty state centres the composer.
- **Content pages:** wrap in `PageShell` (icon, title, one-line description, scrolling body on `canvas-tint`).
- **State shared across views** (chat list, open chat) lives in `features/research/chat-store.tsx`. Keep other state local.
- Every async view has loading (layout-matched `Skeleton`), empty, error (`role="alert"`) and success states.

## Building a UI change: the workflow

1. **Read** `design.md`, `ui-design-guidelines.md` and this file. Skim the nearest existing feature for conventions.
2. **Pick components with the shadcn MCP** before writing markup:
   - `search_items_in_registries` / `list_items_in_registries` to find a component or block,
   - `view_items_in_registries` and `get_item_examples_from_registries` to read source and usage,
   - `get_add_command_for_items` for the install command, then run `npx shadcn@latest add @shadcn/<name>`.
   - If the MCP is not connected, the CLI does the same (`npx shadcn@latest search`, `view`, `add`). Do not recreate a shadcn component by hand.
3. **Use the design skills.** Invoke the `frontend-design` skill for hierarchy and typography choices and the `vercel:shadcn`
   skill for composition and theming. State the reading ("Reading this as: <page> for <audience>...") from the guidelines.
4. **Check what the CLI generated** (see pitfalls). Adjust the new file to the tokens above instead of overriding it at every call site.
5. **Iterate visually with Playwright.** Start the dev server, mock `/api` with `page.route` (reuse `tests/helpers.ts`:
   `withSession`, `json`), screenshot desktop (1440x1000) and mobile (iPhone 13) to the scratchpad, look at the images, fix, repeat.
   Do at least: empty state, populated state, working/loading, error, and the mobile menu. Delete throwaway screenshot specs afterwards.
6. **Verify:** `npm run build` (type-check), `npx oxlint`, `npx playwright test` (desktop and mobile, includes an axe WCAG AA check on each page).
7. **Docs:** a changed design rule needs an edit here or in `design.md` plus a dated entry in `docs/decisions/`, in the same commit.

## Accessibility (enforced by the axe checks)

- Visible `<label>` above inputs (or `sr-only` when the control is self-evident, like the composer). Placeholders are never labels.
- Text on tinted backgrounds must reach 4.5:1. `text-primary` on `bg-primary/10` is for icons only; for text use `text-accent-foreground` on `bg-accent`.
- Everything is keyboard operable with a visible focus ring. Icon-only buttons need `aria-label`. The page keeps a skip link and `main#main-content`.
- Touch targets 36px or more (controls are 36 to 44px).

## Testing conventions

- Every backend call is mocked; tests never reach a real backend or database.
- The sidebar is visible on desktop and inside a sheet on mobile: use `openMenu(page)` and `closeMenu(page)` from `tests/helpers.ts`,
  and scope sidebar checks with `page.locator('[data-testid=sidebar]:visible')` (two copies exist in the DOM on small screens).
- Playwright role queries skip content hidden by an open dialog (`aria-hidden`), so use CSS locators when you must detect the trigger itself.

## Pitfalls we have hit

- **Generated shadcn files can import `cn` from a `cn` npm package.** Change it to `@/lib/utils` and remove the stray dependency.
- **Base UI menus:** `DropdownMenuLabel` must be inside a `DropdownMenuGroup`, otherwise opening the menu crashes the whole page.
- **Button overwrite prompt:** `shadcn add` asks before overwriting `button.tsx`. Answer no (`echo n |`), or it hangs in a non-interactive shell.
- **Radius changes ripple:** `--radius` scales every `rounded-*` token. A large value turns 44px inputs into pills; check inputs after changing it.
- **Escape on a just-opened sheet is ignored** until its animation ends. Tests must retry (see `closeMenu`).
- Use `100dvh` (`h-dvh`) for full-height layouts, never `100vh`.

import { expect, type Page, type Route } from '@playwright/test'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import type axe from 'axe-core'

const require = createRequire(import.meta.url)
export const NOW = '2026-10-13T09:00:00Z'
export const TOKEN = 'tok-1'
export const PASSWORD = 'REDACTED'
export const user = { id: 'u1', email: 'pat.manager@example.com', display_name: 'Pat Manager', role: 'pm' }

export const json = (route: Route, body: unknown, status = 200) => route.fulfill({ status, json: body })
export const authed = (route: Route) => route.request().headers().authorization === `Bearer ${TOKEN}`

export async function noViolations(page: Page) {
  await page.addScriptTag({ path: require.resolve('axe-core/axe.min.js') })
  const violations = await page.evaluate(async () =>
    (await (window as unknown as { axe: typeof axe }).axe.run(document, { runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'] } }))
      .violations.map((v) => ({ id: v.id, nodes: v.nodes.map((n) => n.html.slice(0, 160)) })))
  expect(violations).toEqual([])
}

export async function noOverflow(page: Page) {
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= window.innerWidth)).toBe(true)
}

/** Skip the sign-in form: the token is what the app keeps after a login. */
export async function withSession(page: Page) {
  await page.addInitScript(([k, v]) => window.sessionStorage.setItem(k, v), ['bmw-api-token', TOKEN])
  await page.route('**/api/auth/me', (r) => json(r, user))
  await page.route('**/api/health', (r) => json(r, { status: 'ok', db: 'ok', openai_key: true, version: 'test' }))
}

/** The sidebar is always visible on desktop and lives in a sheet on small screens. */
export async function openMenu(page: Page) {
  const button = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open menu' })
  if (await button.isVisible()) {
    await button.click()
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible()
  }
}
export async function closeMenu(page: Page) {
  // A CSS locator: role queries skip content hidden by the open sheet.
  if (!(await page.locator('button[aria-label="Open menu"]').isVisible())) return
  // Escape is ignored until the sheet has finished opening, so press it again until the sheet is gone.
  await expect(async () => {
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape')
    await expect(page.locator('[data-slot=sheet-content]')).toHaveCount(0, { timeout: 1000 })
  }).toPass()
  await expect(page.locator('#root')).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true')
}

export async function noViolations(page: Page) {

Project: BMW hackathon requirement-evidence engine. Architecture docs live in `docs/`
(start at `docs/README.md`); those `.md` files are the source of truth.

## Repository layout

- `backend/` FastAPI app and Python package `app` (`api/`, `knowledge/`, `agents/`, `ingest/`,
  `orchestration/`), tests in `backend/tests/`. Run with `make backend`, test with `make test`.
- `frontend/` Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui. Run with `make frontend`, build with `make build`.
- `supabase/migrations/` SQL migrations, `docs/` architecture and decisions, `skills/` agent skills,
  `data/` provided BMW files (gitignored). One `.env` at the repo root. See `docs/architecture/12-repo-structure.md`.
- The frontend talks to the backend only through `/api`; it never touches the database directly.
- Put new Python code under `backend/app/`, import it as `app.<package>`, and run scripts as
  `python -m app.<package>.<module>`.

## UI design

- Before generating or changing UI, read `design.md`, `docs/ui-design-guidelines.md` and `docs/frontend-style-guide.md`.
  Find and add components with the shadcn MCP (or `npx shadcn@latest`), use the `frontend-design` skill, and review the
  result in screenshots with Playwright at desktop and mobile sizes before delivering.
- Use the BMW tokens and component rules in `design.md` for all UI.
- Apply the anti-slop workflow in `docs/ui-design-guidelines.md`. BMW's explicit brand rules
  take precedence over generic aesthetic defaults, including white surfaces and the Inter fallback.
  Shape and elevation follow decision 0021 (rounded components, soft shadows), not the rectangular default.

## Database

- Postgres on Supabase (pgvector). To connect, set up a machine or teammate, check the state, apply
  migrations, load data or fix a connection error, read `skills/database-setup/SKILL.md` first.
- Check the connection with `python skills/database-setup/scripts/check_db.py --openai`.
- Never print, log, commit or paste secrets (`SUPABASE_DB_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, passwords, keys).
- **Every API route needs a signed-in user by default.** New routers go into the `protected` router in
  `backend/app/api/__init__.py`. Only `/api/health` and `/api/auth/login` are public; a test checks every route, so do
  not add to the public list without a decision record. Never print or commit tokens or passwords; users are created
  by a human with `python -m app.auth.manage`.
- Agents read evidence through `backend/app/knowledge/tools.py`, not hand-written SQL.

## Pushing

1. **Only push when the user asks.** Never push on your own initiative.
2. **Always squash before pushing.** Collapse all local work since the branch diverged from
   `main` into a single commit (`git reset --soft $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)` then
   commit, or `git merge-base` + `git rebase -i` equivalent without interactive flags). One push
   = one commit.
3. **Commit message:** imperative subject line, then a short body listing what changed and why.
   Mention any `docs/decisions/` entry added or changed.
4. **Never push to `main` directly** unless the user explicitly says so; work on a branch and
   open a PR. Never force-push `main`. Force-pushing your own feature branch after a squash is
   fine (`--force-with-lease`).
5. **Never commit** `data/` (BMW-provided files), `.env`, or any secret. Check `git status`
   before committing; if any of those show up as staged, stop and fix `.gitignore`.

## Docs and design decisions

- When a design decision changes, edit the relevant `docs/architecture/*.md` in place, bump its
  `Last updated` date, and add a dated entry in `docs/decisions/` (see `docs/decisions/README.md`).
  Do this in the same commit as the code change that motivated it.

## Syncing to Supabase after a push

After a successful push, sync the project record to Supabase. Any agent can do this from a shell:

1. Run `python skills/database-setup/scripts/sync_docs.py` from a checkout of the pushed commit. It
   upserts `docs/decisions/*.md` into `design_decisions` and `docs/architecture/*.md` into

# UI design guidelines

Project-specific adaptation of the supplied `design-taste-frontend` guidance.
Read alongside [`../design.md`](../design.md), which defines the BMW design system.

## Scope and precedence

Use BMW tokens for every generated UI. Apply the marketing-page guidance below to landing
pages, portfolios, editorial pages, and redesigns. Do not impose marketing hero, photography,
section variety, or short-copy requirements on the requirement-evidence engine's dashboards,
data tables, agent review screens, or multi-step product workflows. Those screens need clear
information hierarchy, evidence, accessible controls, and complete interaction states.

Explicit user instructions and BMW brand rules override generic taste defaults. In particular:

- Pure white canvas, BMW Blue `#1c69d4`, dark navy hero bands, and 700/300 typography remain.
- Inter is an approved substitute when licensed BMW Type Next Latin is unavailable.
- Components are rounded (`--radius` 0.75rem) with soft `xs`/`sm`/`md` shadows, per [decision 0021](decisions/0021-rounded-chat-first-frontend.md).
  This replaces the earlier rectangular, no-shadow default.
- Light surfaces with dark hero or CTA bands are intentional BMW composition.
- Do not invent a dark theme unless requested; the supplied brand system defines a light base.
- M stripes belong only in M-model or motorsport contexts.

## Before implementation

1. Infer page kind, audience, existing brand, assets, and accessibility constraints.
2. State: "Reading this as: <page kind> for <audience>, with a <vibe> language,
   leaning toward <design system or aesthetic family>."
3. Set `DESIGN_VARIANCE`, `MOTION_INTENSITY`, and `VISUAL_DENSITY` explicitly.
   For measured BMW corporate marketing, start at 4 / 3 / 4; adapt to the brief.
4. For redesigns, audit tokens, information architecture, content, interactions, accessibility,
   analytics, and SEO before editing. Preserve routes, nav labels, form names/order, brand marks,
   and legal/consent copy unless the user authorizes changes.
5. For a specific visual reference, record concrete ratios, spacing, colors, radii, shadows,
   icon treatment, layout structure, and deliberate omissions. Mark estimates as estimates.
   Write a yes/no check for each rule and verify the composition can be rebuilt from the rules.
6. Inspect the existing stack and `package.json` before importing dependencies. Reuse the
   project's foundation; do not mix component systems or recreate an explicitly requested
   official design system by hand.

## Composition and copy

- Use the BMW spacing scale, 80px major section rhythm, 24px card padding, and 1440px container.
- Prefer purposeful alignment and real content hierarchy over decorative asymmetry.
- Marketing heroes: at most two desktop headline lines, 20 words of supporting copy,
  one primary and at most one secondary CTA. Keep CTAs visible in the initial viewport.
  Limit desktop top padding to 96px and hero text to four elements total.
- Keep desktop navigation on one line and 64px tall, with an 80px maximum.
- Use at most one section eyebrow per three marketing sections. Avoid numbered sections,
  scroll cues, version stamps, decorative status dots, atmospheric locale strips, and
  decoration text at the hero's bottom.
- Avoid repeated generic feature-card rows, empty bento cells, and three consecutive
  alternating image/text splits. Choose layouts that fit the actual content.
- Put supporting paragraphs directly below headings; avoid floating corner explainers.
- Keep marketing paragraphs short and quotes within three lines. Use disclosures, grouped
  content, or separate pages for long lists rather than dumping data into landing pages.
- Use plain, grammatical copy. Avoid forced metaphors, filler verbs, invented testimonials,
  fabricated metrics, and fake precision. Label sample data explicitly.
- Use one label per CTA intent and one verb per action throughout the product.
- Generated visible UI copy uses regular hyphens, commas, periods, or parentheses instead
  of em-dashes or en-dash separators. Preserve supplied source material as supplied.

## Assets and styling

- Use real brand assets and real component previews. Never fabricate screenshot-like
  rectangles, terminal windows, or dashboards as decorative product previews.
- For marketing surfaces needing photography, prefer suitable generated assets when tools
  are available, then verified real imagery. If assets cannot be obtained, use clearly marked
  placeholders and report the missing placements. Product workflows do not need stock imagery.
- Use real logos for genuine social proof; do not invent customers or decorative photo credits.
- Keep images free of decorative pills and labels. Reserve dimensions to prevent layout shifts.
- Use one icon family. Prefer Phosphor, HugeIcons, Radix, or Tabler; retain Lucide if already
  used by the project. Do not hand-draw SVG icon paths.
- Avoid gradient text, glows, glass panels, random accent colors, custom cursors, and ornamental
  grid lines. BMW photography and surface contrast provide depth.
- Self-host fonts with `font-display: swap`, or use `next/font` in Next.js.

## Interaction and engineering

- Provide meaningful loading, empty, error, disabled, selected, focus, and success states
  where the interaction requires them. Use layout-matched skeletons for loading.
- Put labels above form inputs, helper text alongside the field, and inline errors below.
  Placeholders are never labels. Ensure keyboard operation and visible focus.
- Check text, placeholders, focus indicators, and controls for WCAG AA contrast. Keep CTA
  labels on one desktop line and touch targets at least 48px where BMW specifies them.
- Use CSS Grid for grids and declare each multi-column layout's mobile collapse explicitly.
  Use `min-height: 100dvh` when a full-height layout is needed, rather than fixed `100vh`.
- Keep state local unless shared state is necessary. Put providers and interactive islands
  in Client Components in Next.js; static layouts can remain Server Components.
- Animate only when motion explains hierarchy, feedback, storytelling, or state changes.
  Honor reduced motion. Do not claim motion that has not been implemented.
- Use Motion values for continuous pointer/scroll values, never React state. Avoid raw scroll
  listeners. Use IntersectionObserver, CSS scroll animations, Motion, or GSAP ScrollTrigger.
- Isolate animation code in client leaves and clean up effects. Do not let animation libraries
  compete over the same elements. Keep marquees to at most one per marketing page.
- For actual GSAP pinned stacks or horizontal pans, pin at `start: "top top"` and use correct
  end distances and scrub behavior. Do not add scroll hijacks merely for decoration.
- Keep z-index layers intentional, lazy-load heavy below-the-fold code, and avoid grain filters
  on scrolling containers. Target LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, and CLS < 0.1.

## Pre-flight before delivery

Check applicable rules; mark out-of-scope items as such rather than inventing content to satisfy
them. Fix failures before delivering and report any checks that could not be run.

- Brief, mode, dials, reference rules, and BMW precedence are explicit.
- Colors, fonts, radii, spacing, and component states match `design.md`.

- Section layouts and eyebrow counts fit the marketing composition, with no empty filler cells.
- Assets load, previews are real, and social proof has a factual basis.
- Buttons, inputs, text, focus states, keyboard paths, and touch targets pass accessibility checks.
- Loading, empty, error, and disabled states work for relevant interactions.
- Motion is motivated, implemented, cleaned up, and disabled or simplified under reduced motion.
- Test every supported theme; do not require an invented theme merely to satisfy a generic rule.

  pages, run Lighthouse when a runnable browser environment is available; report measured
  results honestly instead of asserting Core Web Vitals from code inspection alone.
# Frontend style guide

How the frontend is built and changed. Read with [`../design.md`](../design.md) (brand tokens),
[`ui-design-guidelines.md`](ui-design-guidelines.md) (anti-slop workflow) and
[decision 0021](decisions/0021-rounded-chat-first-frontend.md) (rounded, chat-first look).
Where they disagree, 0021 wins on shape and elevation; `design.md` wins on colour and type.

## Stack

Vite, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui (style `base-nova`, **Base UI** primitives, not Radix), lucide icons.
Components live in `frontend/src/components/ui/`, features in `src/features/<name>/`, shared chrome in
`src/components/layout/`. The UI talks only to `/api` through `src/lib/api.ts`.

## Look and feel

| Aspect | Rule |
|---|---|
| Colour | White canvas, `canvas-tint` (#f6f7f9) behind white cards. BMW Blue (`primary`) is the only action colour. Semantic colours only for state. No gradients, glows, glass. |
| Type | Inter Variable. Body 400, headings 600, no negative tracking beyond `-0.01em` on headings. |
| Shape | `--radius` 0.75rem. Cards `rounded-2xl`, inputs and buttons `rounded-xl`, chat bubbles and composer `rounded-3xl`, chips and avatars pills. |
| Elevation | `shadow-xs` on cards, `shadow-sm` on primary buttons, `shadow-md` on the composer and sign-in panel only. |
| Icons | lucide only, `size-4` inline, `size-5` in headings. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden`. Never hand-draw SVG. |
| Spacing | 4px scale. Page gutters `px-4 sm:px-8`. Chat column `max-w-3xl`, pages `max-w-6xl`. |
| Motion | Only `.rise` (new messages) and `.typing-dot`. Both are disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`. |
| Copy | Plain sentences, no em or en dashes, one verb per action ("Send", "Search", "Sign out"). No invented data: examples are labelled as examples. |

## Layout patterns

- **Shell:** `App.tsx` holds a 288px sidebar (`components/layout/Sidebar.tsx`) and the main column. Below `md` the sidebar is a `Sheet`.
- **Chat view:** `h-dvh` column, scrolling thread, composer pinned at the bottom. The empty state centres the composer.
- **Content pages:** wrap in `PageShell` (icon, title, one-line description, scrolling body on `canvas-tint`).
- **State shared across views** (chat list, open chat) lives in `features/research/chat-store.tsx`. Keep other state local.
- Every async view has loading (layout-matched `Skeleton`), empty, error (`role="alert"`) and success states.

## Building a UI change: the workflow

1. **Read** `design.md`, `ui-design-guidelines.md` and this file. Skim the nearest existing feature for conventions.
2. **Pick components with the shadcn MCP** before writing markup:
   - `search_items_in_registries` / `list_items_in_registries` to find a component or block,
   - `view_items_in_registries` and `get_item_examples_from_registries` to read source and usage,
   - `get_add_command_for_items` for the install command, then run `npx shadcn@latest add @shadcn/<name>`.
   - If the MCP is not connected, the CLI does the same (`npx shadcn@latest search`, `view`, `add`). Do not recreate a shadcn component by hand.
3. **Use the design skills.** Invoke the `frontend-design` skill for hierarchy and typography choices and the `vercel:shadcn`
   skill for composition and theming. State the reading ("Reading this as: <page> for <audience>...") from the guidelines.
4. **Check what the CLI generated** (see pitfalls). Adjust the new file to the tokens above instead of overriding it at every call site.
5. **Iterate visually with Playwright.** Start the dev server, mock `/api` with `page.route` (reuse `tests/helpers.ts`:
   `withSession`, `json`), screenshot desktop (1440x1000) and mobile (iPhone 13) to the scratchpad, look at the images, fix, repeat.
   Do at least: empty state, populated state, working/loading, error, and the mobile menu. Delete throwaway screenshot specs afterwards.
6. **Verify:** `npm run build` (type-check), `npx oxlint`, `npx playwright test` (desktop and mobile, includes an axe WCAG AA check on each page).
7. **Docs:** a changed design rule needs an edit here or in `design.md` plus a dated entry in `docs/decisions/`, in the same commit.

## Accessibility (enforced by the axe checks)

- Visible `<label>` above inputs (or `sr-only` when the control is self-evident, like the composer). Placeholders are never labels.
- Text on tinted backgrounds must reach 4.5:1. `text-primary` on `bg-primary/10` is for icons only; for text use `text-accent-foreground` on `bg-accent`.
- Everything is keyboard operable with a visible focus ring. Icon-only buttons need `aria-label`. The page keeps a skip link and `main#main-content`.
- Touch targets 36px or more (controls are 36 to 44px).

## Testing conventions

- Every backend call is mocked; tests never reach a real backend or database.
- The sidebar is visible on desktop and inside a sheet on mobile: use `openMenu(page)` and `closeMenu(page)` from `tests/helpers.ts`,
  and scope sidebar checks with `page.locator('[data-testid=sidebar]:visible')` (two copies exist in the DOM on small screens).
- Playwright role queries skip content hidden by an open dialog (`aria-hidden`), so use CSS locators when you must detect the trigger itself.

## Pitfalls we have hit

- **Generated shadcn files can import `cn` from a `cn` npm package.** Change it to `@/lib/utils` and remove the stray dependency.
- **Base UI menus:** `DropdownMenuLabel` must be inside a `DropdownMenuGroup`, otherwise opening the menu crashes the whole page.
- **Button overwrite prompt:** `shadcn add` asks before overwriting `button.tsx`. Answer no (`echo n |`), or it hangs in a non-interactive shell.
- **Radius changes ripple:** `--radius` scales every `rounded-*` token. A large value turns 44px inputs into pills; check inputs after changing it.
- **Escape on a just-opened sheet is ignored** until its animation ends. Tests must retry (see `closeMenu`).
- Use `100dvh` (`h-dvh`) for full-height layouts, never `100vh`.

# 0021 — Chat-first frontend with rounded components and soft elevation

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted · Amends the shape and elevation rules of [`design.md`](../../design.md) and [`ui-design-guidelines.md`](../ui-design-guidelines.md); builds on [0017](0017-minimal-live-only-frontend.md)

## Context

The frontend looked like a plain document site: a top bar, a text-only conversation list beside the thread, and
rectangular, hairline-bordered components. The product is a research conversation, so it should read like a modern
chat app. The user asked explicitly for rounded edges, icons, and chat history on the left.

## Decision

1. **Layout.** A left sidebar (fixed on desktop, a sheet below `md`) holds the brand, New chat, the three views, the
   chat history grouped by recency, the account menu and the backend status. The Research view is a centred thread with
   a rounded composer, an empty state with example questions, and a typing indicator while an agent works.
2. **Shape.** `--radius` is 0.75rem. Cards, inputs, buttons and menus are rounded; chips and avatars are pills.
   This overrides the "rectangular components" default in `design.md`.
3. **Elevation.** Three soft shadow tokens (`xs`, `sm`, `md`) replace "no drop shadows"; they are used only on the composer,
   cards and the sign-in panel. Depth otherwise still comes from surface contrast (`canvas-tint` behind white cards).
4. **Unchanged brand rules.** BMW Blue stays the only action colour, white canvas, Inter as the substitute typeface, light
   theme only, no gradients or glows. Body weight is now 400 and headings 600 (was 300 and 700) for legibility in dense chat text.
5. **One icon family** (lucide, already in the project) and shadcn components on Base UI (`avatar`, `dropdown-menu`,
   `scroll-area`, `sheet`, `tooltip`).

## Consequences

Brand fidelity to BMW's corporate site is looser on purpose; the product is an internal tool, not a marketing page.
Tests that reach the sidebar open the sheet first on small screens (`openMenu` and `closeMenu` in `tests/helpers.ts`).

# 0021 — Chat-first frontend with rounded components and soft elevation

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted · Amends the shape and elevation rules of [`design.md`](../../design.md) and [`ui-design-guidelines.md`](../ui-design-guidelines.md); builds on [0017](0017-minimal-live-only-frontend.md)

## Context

The frontend looked like a plain document site: a top bar, a text-only conversation list beside the thread, and
rectangular, hairline-bordered components. The product is a research conversation, so it should read like a modern
chat app. The user asked explicitly for rounded edges, icons, and chat history on the left.

## Decision

1. **Layout.** A left sidebar (fixed on desktop, a sheet below `md`) holds the brand, New chat, the three views, the
   chat history grouped by recency, the account menu and the backend status. The Research view is a centred thread with
   a rounded composer, an empty state with example questions, and a typing indicator while an agent works.
2. **Shape.** `--radius` is 0.75rem. Cards, inputs, buttons and menus are rounded; chips and avatars are pills.
   This overrides the "rectangular components" default in `design.md`.
3. **Elevation.** Three soft shadow tokens (`xs`, `sm`, `md`) replace "no drop shadows"; they are used only on the composer,
   cards and the sign-in panel. Depth otherwise still comes from surface contrast (`canvas-tint` behind white cards).
4. **Unchanged brand rules.** BMW Blue stays the only action colour, white canvas, Inter as the substitute typeface, light
   theme only, no gradients or glows. Body weight is now 400 and headings 600 (was 300 and 700) for legibility in dense chat text.
5. **One icon family** (lucide, already in the project) and shadcn components on Base UI (`avatar`, `dropdown-menu`,
   `scroll-area`, `sheet`, `tooltip`).

## Consequences

Brand fidelity to BMW's corporate site is looser on purpose; the product is an internal tool, not a marketing page.
Tests that reach the sidebar open the sheet first on small screens (`openMenu` and `closeMenu` in `tests/helpers.ts`).

# 0022 — Optional-feature market impact as explicit scenarios

> Date: 2026-10-10 · Status: accepted · Builds on 0017 and 0021

## Context

The user requested a map showing whether a chosen optional feature positively or negatively affects share in each
market. The knowledge layer contains equipment availability, feedback and sales volumes, but no validated causal
feature-to-share model or option adoption baseline. Coloring countries with inferred numeric forecasts would
misrepresent that evidence.

## Decision

Add a Market impact view to the existing authenticated frontend. Read cited optional equipment using a new protected
`GET /api/market-impact/options?line=` route over `knowledge.tools.get_options`, bounded at 200 options with an explicit
truncation flag. Allow a clearly labeled custom feature if catalog evidence is absent.

The user enters market-share changes in percentage points and optional baseline shares. Positive, negative, zero
and unassessed values have distinct map colors and text labels. Validate numbers and resulting shares; do not
silently clamp them or turn missing assumptions into zero. The inclusion switch sets the feature's effect to zero
while preserving assumptions for comparison. Isolate scenarios by feature and vehicle line, keep them in memory,
and offer a JSON export containing assumptions, calculated results, and the selected catalog citation.

Use public-domain Natural Earth country geometry, preprojected into a local asset. The map applies each business
market assumption to its whole schematic group: Europe excluding Russia (EU), China, United States, or rest of world.
Document that grouping next to the map and in the export. Keep equivalent market buttons for keyboard use and text
labels for users who cannot distinguish the colors. Keep BMW tokens, rounded shadcn controls and the current shell.

## Consequences

The map is usable without fabricating forecasts and without a map service or runtime geometry dependency. It needs
no schema migration. Catalog outages remain visible and custom scenarios remain usable. Values are not saved to the
server and leaving the view discards them unless exported. A future prediction model must define its inputs,
calibration, uncertainty and evidence before it can replace the scenario assumptions. This decision amends the
frontend boundary in `docs/architecture/12-repo-structure.md`.
